Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 3, verse 1–6:

It is Medinan.

{1} {Alif-Lam-Mim}: from the letters whose meaning none knows except Allah.

{2} He, exalted is He, informs that He is {the Ever-Living}: perfect in life, {the Sustainer}: who subsists by Himself and sustains the conditions of His creation. He has established their religious conditions, their worldly conditions and their decreed conditions. He sent down to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) the Book with the truth, which contains no doubt and comprises truth.

{3-4} {Confirming what came before it} of the Books: that is, it bears witness to what they bore witness to, agrees with them, and confirms the messengers who brought them. Likewise, {He sent down the Torah and the Gospel before} this Book, {as guidance for mankind}. He completed and sealed the message with Muhammad (ﷺ), and with his great Book through which Allah guided creation out of misguidance and rescued them through it from ignorance, and by which He distinguished between truth and falsehood, happiness and wretchedness, the straight path and the paths of Hellfire. As for those who believed in it and were guided by it, they attained through it abundant good and reward, both immediate and deferred. As for {those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah}, which He made clear in His Book and upon the tongue of His Messenger, {they will have a severe punishment, and Allah is Exalted in Might, the Lord of Retribution} against whoever disobeys Him.

{5-6} And part of the completeness of His sustaining (qayyumiyyah) is that His knowledge encompasses all creatures: {nothing on earth or in heaven is hidden from Him}, even what is in the wombs of pregnant women. He is {the One who forms you in the wombs as He wills}: male or female, complete in creation or incomplete, passing through the stages of His creation and the wonders of His wisdom. Whoever has this relationship with His servants, and this great care for their affairs from the time He brings them into being until the end of their matters, having no partner in that, it is necessarily established that none deserves worship except Him: {there is no deity except Him, the Almighty}, who subdued creation by His power and is exalted above being described with any deficiency or characterized by any blame, {the Wise} in His creation and His legislation.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 3, verse 7–8:

{7} He, may He be exalted, informs of His greatness and the perfection of His self-subsistence (qayyumiyyah), that He alone sent down this great Book, the like of which has not existed and no equal or near equal will ever exist in its guidance, its eloquence, its inimitability, and its reform of creation. This Book contains the muhkam (clear, decisive verses) whose meanings are plain and evident, not confused with anything else. Among it are also the mutashabih (ambiguous verses) which admit of several meanings, and none of the two possibilities is specified by them alone until they are joined to the muhkam. Those in whose hearts is sickness, deviation and swerving, due to their bad intention, follow the mutashabih of it, and they argue from it for their false statements and their deceptive opinions, seeking discord and distorting His Book, and interpreting it according to their tendencies and schools, so that they may go astray and lead others astray.

As for the firmly grounded in knowledge (al-rasikhun fi al-'ilm), those in whose hearts knowledge and certainty have reached, and whose knowledge and understanding have borne fruit in action, they know that the whole Qur'an is from Allah, and that all of it is truth, its muhkam and its mutashabih alike, and that truth does not contradict or differ. Because they know that the muhkam verses have meanings in the utmost clarity and explicitness, they refer back to them the mushtabih (unclear matters) in which bewilderment occurs for one of deficient knowledge and deficient understanding. Thus they refer the mutashabih to the muhkam, and it all becomes muhkam, and they say: ﴿We believe in it; all is from our Lord﴾; and ﴿none will be reminded except those of understanding﴾ — that is, the people of sound intellect; for beneficial matters and correct sciences. In this is evidence that this is a sign of the people of understanding, and that following the mutashabih is among the attributes of people of corrupt opinions, weak intellects and evil intentions.

As for His saying: ﴿And none knows its interpretation except Allah﴾: if by "interpretation" (ta'wil) is meant knowing the final outcome of matters and what they end up being, then stopping at ﴿except Allah﴾ is required, since He, may He be exalted, alone knows the ta'wil in this sense. If by ta'wil is meant tafsir (exegesis) and knowing the meaning of the speech, then conjoining (the phrase to what follows) is preferable; and this is then praise of the firmly grounded in knowledge, that they know how to apply the texts of the Book and the Sunnah, their muhkam and their mutashabih.

When the context was one of division into deviators and upright ones, they called upon Allah, may He be exalted, to keep them firm in faith, and they said:

{8} ﴿Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us﴾; that is, do not incline them away from the truth toward falsehood, ﴿and grant us from Yourself mercy﴾ by which our circumstances may be set right; ﴿indeed, You are the Bestower﴾; that is, abundant in grace and gifts. This verse serves as an example of the method that must be followed regarding the mutashabih. Allah, may He be exalted, mentioned of the firmly grounded that they ask Him not to let their hearts swerve after He has guided them; and He has informed in other verses of the causes by which the hearts of the people of deviation swerve, and that this is due to their own earning, such as His saying: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾; ﴿Then they turned away; Allah turned their hearts away﴾; ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights, as they did not believe in it the first time﴾. So when the servant turns away from his Lord, allies with His enemy, sees the truth and turns from it, sees falsehood and chooses it, Allah leaves him to what he has chosen for himself, and turns his heart away as a punishment for his deviation. Allah did not wrong him, but he wronged himself, so let him blame none but his commanding self (nafs ammarah bi al-su'). And Allah knows best.

This entails its requirement and consequence in action and preparation for that Day, for belief in the Resurrection and recompense is the root of the soundness of hearts, and the root of desire for good and fear of evil, which are the foundation of all good.

{10–11} When He mentioned the Day of Resurrection, He mentioned that all who disbelieve in Allah and deny His messengers will certainly enter the Fire and burn in it, and that their wealth and their children will not avail them anything against the punishment of Allah. He also mentioned that there will befall them in this world the seizings and punishments that befell Pharaoh and the rest of the nations that denied the signs of Allah: ﴿Allah seized them for their sins﴾. This is a report and a glad tiding to the believers, and a warning to the disbelievers, that they will inevitably be overcome in this world. And it occurred just as God had informed: they were defeated with a defeat for which there was no like or equal. God, exalted is He, made what occurred at Badr one of His signs indicating the truthfulness of His Messenger, and that he is upon the truth while his enemies are upon falsehood. When the two groups met, the group of the believers numbered no more than three hundred and some ten men, with their small number of equipment, while the group of the disbelievers approached a thousand, with their complete readiness in weapons and otherwise. So God supported the believers with His help, and they defeated them by God's permission. In this there is a lesson for people of insight (ahl al-basa'ir), for were it not that this is the truth which, when it confronts falsehood, destroys it, and falsehood vanishes, then by the material causes the matter would have been the reverse.

Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 3, verses 14–15:

{14} In these two verses, God, exalted is He, informs us about the state of people in preferring the worldly life over the Hereafter, and He clarifies the great disparity and the vast difference between the two abodes. He informs us that these things have been made attractive to people: they gaze upon them with their eyes, they deem them lawful in their hearts, and souls are devoted to their pleasures. Every group of people inclines toward one type of these things, having made them their greatest concern and the sum of their knowledge. Yet, despite this, they are a little enjoyment that passes away within a short time. This is {the enjoyment of the worldly life, while with God is the best return}.

{15} Then He informs us about this: that those who are mindful of God and who devote themselves to His worship are better than these pleasures. For them are kinds of good things and lasting bliss, of which {no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and it has not occurred to any human heart}. For them is the good pleasure of God, which is greater than everything. For them are {purified spouses}, purified from every blemish and deficiency, beautiful in character and perfect in qualities, because negation implies its opposite; purifying them from blemishes necessitates describing them with perfections. {And God is Seeing of the servants}; so He facilitates for each of them what they were created for. As for the people of happiness, He makes them ready for works of this everlasting abode, and they take from this worldly life what helps them in worshipping God and obeying Him. As for the people of wretchedness and aversion, He destines them to the deeds of the people of wretchedness, and they are content with the worldly life, find rest in it, and take it as a dwelling place.

{16} That is: these, those firmly rooted in knowledge, the people of knowledge and faith, seek a means (tawassul) to their Lord through their faith, asking for the forgiveness of their sins and protection from the punishment of the Fire. This is among the means that Allah loves, that a servant seek a means to his Lord through what He has bestowed upon him of faith and righteous deeds, in order to perfect Allah's blessings upon him by attaining complete reward and the averting of punishment.

{17} Then He described them with the most beautiful attributes: with patience (sabr), which is restraining the souls upon what Allah loves, seeking His good pleasure. They are patient in obedience to Allah, patient in refraining from His disobedience, and patient in His painful decrees. And with truthfulness (sidq) in words and conditions, which is the evenness of the outward and the inward, and the sincerity of resolve in following the Straight Path. And with devotion (qunut), which is the continuance of obedience accompanied by humility and submission. And with spending (nafaqat) in the paths of good and upon the poor and those in need. And with seeking forgiveness (istighfar), especially at the time of the pre-dawn hours (al-asḥar), for they extended their prayer until the time of dawn, then sat seeking forgiveness from Allah, the Exalted.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 3, verse 18:

{18} This is the greatest of testimonies, issued by the Mighty King, by the angels, and by people of knowledge (ahl al-'ilm), concerning the most exalted thing testified to, which is the Oneness of God (tawhid Allah) and His standing upright in justice (qiyam bil-qist). This includes testimony to the entire Sharia and all the rulings of recompense. The Sharia and the religion have as their root and foundation the Oneness of God, the singling out of Him in worship, and the acknowledgment that He alone possesses the attributes of greatness, pride, glory, might, power and majesty, and the descriptions of generosity, kindness, mercy, benevolence and beauty, and His absolute perfection, of which no creature can encompass any part, reach it, or attain to praising Him. The legal acts of worship, the transactions and their consequences, and the commands and prohibitions are all justice and equity, with no injustice or oppression in them in any respect; rather, they are in the utmost wisdom and soundness. And the recompense for good and evil deeds is all equity and justice. ﴿Say: What thing is greatest in testimony? Say: God﴾. Thus the Oneness of God, His religion and His recompense are established beyond any doubt, and they are the greatest and clearest of realities. God has established for this proofs and evidences that cannot be counted or enumerated.

In this verse is the virtue of knowledge and of the people of knowledge, for God singled them out for mention above mankind, joined their testimony with His testimony and that of His angels, and made their testimony among the greatest proofs and evidences of His Oneness, His religion and His recompense. It is obligatory upon the responsible (mukallafun) to accept this just and truthful testimony. Implicit in this is their being declared trustworthy (ta'dil), that the creation follows them, and that they are the leaders and those who are followed. In this is virtue, honour and elevation of station beyond measure.

{19} He, exalted is He, informs us that {Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam}; that is, the religion besides which Allah has no other religion and accepts no other is {Islam}, which is submission to Allah alone, outwardly and inwardly, by what He has legislated through the tongues of His messengers. The Exalted said: {And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him, and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers}. So whoever adheres to a religion other than the religion of Islam has not truly submitted to Allah, because he has not followed the path that He legislated through the tongues of His messengers.

Then He, exalted is He, informs us that the People of the Book know this, and that they only differed and deviated from it out of obstinacy and tyranny. Otherwise, knowledge had come to them that required there be no disagreement and that necessitated adherence to the true religion. Then, when Muhammad (ﷺ) came to them, they recognized him with true recognition, but envy, tyranny, and disbelief in the signs of Allah are what prevented them from following the truth. {And whoever disbelieves in the signs of Allah, then indeed Allah is swift in reckoning}; that is, let them await that, for it is coming, and Allah will surely recompense them for what they used to do.

{20} When he had explained that the true religion with Allah is Islam, and the People of the Book had debated with the Prophet (ﷺ) face to face, and the proof had been established against them but they obstinately rejected it, Allah the Exalted then commanded him to say and declare that he has submitted his face, that is, his outward and inward self, to Allah, and that whoever follows him in this has agreed with him in this pure submission. He was also to say to all people, both the People of the Book and the unlettered (al-ummiyyin), that is, those who have no scripture, from the Arabs and others: "If you submit, then you are upon the straight path, the guidance and the truth; but if you turn away, then your reckoning is with Allah, and I have no duty except to convey (the message). I have conveyed it to you, and the proof has been established against you."

{21–22} That is: those who combined these evils: disbelief in the signs of Allah, denial of the messengers of Allah, and grave transgression against the greatest of creation in their right over the creation, namely the messengers and the imams of guidance, who command people to justice (al-qist), which both the religions and the intellects agree upon. Those have {their deeds rendered void in this world and the Hereafter}; they deserve painful punishment, and they have no helper against the punishment of Allah, nor any rescuer from His retribution.

{23–25} That is: Do you not look and marvel at these people, "who were given a portion of the Scripture," and who are called "to the Book of God," which confirms what He sent down to His messengers? Yet "a faction of them turn away, while they are averse," from following the truth. It is as if it were said: What caused them to call to this aversion, when they are most deserving of following and most knowing of the reality of what Muhammad (ﷺ) brought? For this, he mentions two causes.

The first: their security and their false testimony for themselves that they will be saved, and that the Fire will touch them only "for a number of days" which they have fixed according to their corrupt desires, as if the governance of the kingdom returned to them, when they said: "None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians." It is well known that these are false wishes, invalid both by the Sharia and by reason.

The second cause: when they denied the signs of God and fabricated lies against Him, Satan made the evil of their deeds appear fair to them, and they were deceived by that, and it appeared to them as the truth, as a punishment for them for their turning away from the truth. So how will their condition be when God gathers them on the Day of Resurrection, and pays those who worked what they did, and the justice of God takes its course among His servants? Then you will not ask about the punishment they will reach and the good and reward that will escape them. That is "because of what their hands have earned, and your Lord is not unjust to the servants."

{26–27} God commands His Prophet (ﷺ) primarily, and others by extension, to say on behalf of his Lord, declaring His sole control over affairs and His management of the upper and lower worlds, and His entitlement, by virtue of His exclusive possession of absolute sovereignty and perfectly firm disposal, that He gives dominion to whom He wills, strips dominion from whom He wills, honors whom He wills, and abases whom He wills. Thus the matter is not by the wishful thinking (amani) of the People of the Book or of anyone else; rather the matter is God's matter, and the governance belongs to Him. There is no opponent to His governance, nor any helper in His decree.

And just as He is the one who disposes of the alternation of days among people, He is also the one who disposes of time itself: "He makes the night pass into the day and makes the day pass into the night" (yulij al-nahar fi al-layl wa yulij al-layl fi al-nahar); that is, He causes this to enter upon that, this to take the place of that, and adds to this what He takes from that, so as to establish thereby the welfare of His creatures. "And He brings forth the living from the dead" (wa yukhriju al-hayy min al-mayyit), just as He brings forth crops and varied trees from their seeds, and the believer from the disbeliever, and the dead from the living, just as He brings forth grains, date-stones, crops, trees, and the chick from the egg. He is the one who brings forth opposites from one another, and all the elements have submitted to Him.

As for His saying, "In Your hand is the good" (bi-yadika al-khayr): that is, all good is from You, and none brings good deeds and goodness except God. As for evil, it is not attributed to God, Exalted is He, neither as a description, nor as a name, nor as an act. Rather, it enters within His created effects and is included in His decree and destiny. So good and evil all fall within His decree and destiny; nothing occurs in His dominion except what He wills. But evil is not attributed to God; so it is not said, "In Your hand is the good and the evil," but rather, "In Your hand is the good," as God said and as His Messenger said. As for the qualification of some exegetes who said, "Likewise, evil is in the hand of God," it is pure error; their basis was their supposition that singling out good for mention contradicts His general decree and destiny. The answer to that is what we have explained.

As for His saying, "And You provide whom You will without reckoning" (wa tarzuqu man tasha'u bi-ghayri hisab): God has mentioned in other verses the means by which His provision is obtained, such as His saying: "And whoever fears God, He will make for him a way out and provide for him from where he does not expect" (Q 65:2–3), and "And whoever relies upon God, then He is sufficient for him" (Q 65:3). So the servants must seek provision only from God, and strive for it by the means that God has facilitated and permitted.

This is a prohibition from Allah and a warning to the believers against taking the disbelievers as allies (awliya') instead of the believers, for the believers are allies of one another, and Allah is their Protector (wali). {And whoever does that}, that is, takes them as allies, {then he has nothing to do with Allah}; i.e., he is free of Allah, and Allah is free of him, as in His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And whoever among you takes them as allies, then indeed he is one of them﴾. And His words: ﴿Except when you fear a danger from them﴾; i.e., except when you fear for yourselves in showing enmity toward the disbelievers. In this case you have a concession (rukhsah) to show peaceful relations and truce (musalamah wa muhadanah), but not to take them as allies, which is love of the heart that is followed by support. ﴿And Allah warns you of Himself﴾; i.e., so fear Him, be in awe of Him, and give His fear precedence over the fear of people, for He is the One who manages the affairs of the servants, has taken hold of their forelocks, and to Him they will return and be brought back. He will reward with abundant reward those who give precedence to fearing and hoping in Him over anything else, and He will punish the disbelievers and those who take them as allies with a severe torment.

{29–30} He, exalted is He, informs that His knowledge encompasses what is in the breasts, whether the servants conceal it or disclose it, just as His knowledge encompasses everything in the heavens and the earth, so that nothing is hidden from Him. Together with the comprehensiveness of His knowledge, He is the Mighty, the All-Powerful over everything, whose will cannot be thwarted by any existing thing. Having mentioned to them of His greatness and the vastness of His attributes what necessitates that the servants be mindful of Him in all their states, He also mentioned to them another call to be mindful of Him and to be wary of Him: that they will all return to Him, and their deeds, whether good or evil, will then be presented. Then the people of goodness will rejoice in what they have sent forward for themselves, and the people of evil will regret when they find what they had done presented, and they will wish that between them and it there were a far distance.

When the servant knows that he is striving toward his Lord and toiling in this life, and that he must meet his Lord and meet his striving, this obliges him to take caution and guard against deeds that bring disgrace and punishment, and to prepare with righteous deeds that bring happiness and reward. For this reason, He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And Allah warns you of Himself﴾; that is, through what He makes manifest to you of the attributes of His greatness, the perfection of His justice, and the severity of His punishment. Yet despite the severity of His punishment, He is Kind and Merciful. Among His kindness and mercy is that He instilled fear in the servants and restrained them from error and corruption, as He said when mentioning the punishments: ﴿That is what Allah frightens His servants with. O My servants, so fear Me﴾. Thus His kindness and mercy made easy for them the paths by which they attain good things, and His kindness and mercy warned them against the paths that lead them to what is disliked.

So we ask Him, exalted is He, to complete His favor upon us by following the Straight Path and being safe from the paths that lead their travelers to the Hellfire.

{31–32} This verse is the criterion by which one can recognize who truly loves Allah and who merely claims it without substance. The sign of the love of Allah is following Muhammad (ﷺ), who made following him and all that he calls to into a path to the love of Allah and His good pleasure. Thus the love of Allah, His good pleasure and His reward are attained only by affirming what the Messenger brought from the Book and the Sunnah, carrying out their commands and avoiding their prohibitions. Whoever does this, Allah loves him, rewards him as He rewards those who love Him, forgives his sins and covers over his faults. It is as if it were said: "Along with that, what is the reality of following the Messenger and its description?" So He answered with His saying: ﴿Say: Obey Allah and the Messenger﴾, by carrying out the command, avoiding the prohibition, and affirming the report; ﴿but if they turn away﴾ from that, then this is disbelief, and ﴿Allah does not love the disbelievers﴾.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 3, verse 33–55:

{33–55} Allah, exalted is He, has among His servants chosen ones (asfiya'), whom He selects, chooses, and bestows upon with lofty virtues, sublime attributes, beneficial knowledge, righteous deeds, and diverse distinctions. He mentioned these great households and what they contained of perfected men (kummal al-rijal) who attained the qualities of perfection, and that virtue and goodness continued in their offspring, encompassing both their males and their females. This is among His greatest favours and the finest objects of His generosity and munificence. {And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing}: He knows who deserves virtue and preference, and He places His bounty where His wisdom requires. 

When He established the greatness of these households, He mentioned the story of Maryam and her son Isa (ﷺ), and how the two of them descended from these virtuous households, and how their circumstances shifted from the beginning of their affair to its end. The wife of 'Imran said, humbly supplicating her Lord and drawing near to Him by this act which He loves, which includes the magnification of His House and constant obedience to Him: {Indeed, I have dedicated to You what is in my womb, consecrated (muharraran)}; that is, a servant to the house of worship, filled with those who worship. {So accept it from me}; that is, make this deed founded upon faith and sincerity, bearing fruit of good and reward. {Indeed, You are the All-Hearing, All-Knowing.} {So when she delivered her, she said, "My Lord, I have delivered a female," and Allah was most knowing of what she delivered, "and the male is not like the female."}

It was as if in this statement there was a kind of humble supplication and brokenness of soul, since her vow had been based on the expectation that the child would be a male, who would possess the strength, service, and capacity for this task that people of strength possess, whereas a female is different in this regard. So Allah consoled her heart and accepted her vow, and this female became more perfect and complete than many males, indeed than most of them, and greater objectives were attained through her than through a male. Therefore He said: {So her Lord accepted her with good acceptance and caused her to grow in a good growth}; that is, she was raised with a wondrous upbringing—religious, moral, and cultured—through which her circumstances were perfected, her words and deeds were made righteous, and her perfection flourished. Allah facilitated for her Zakariya as guardian, and this is among Allah's favours upon a servant: that He makes whoever takes charge of his upbringing one of the perfected and reforming.

Then Allah honoured Maryam and Zakariya, in that He made easy for Maryam a provision that came without toil or hardship, and it was purely a dignity with which Allah honoured her, since {whenever Zakariya entered upon her the sanctuary (mihrab)}, which is the place of worship, and this indicates her frequent prayer and constant presence in her sanctuary, {he found with her provision}, ready and prepared. He said: {"From where is this for you?" She said, "It is from Allah. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without account."} When Zakariya saw this state and the righteousness and kindness of Allah toward her, it reminded him to ask Allah for a child in a time of despair regarding it, so he said: {"My Lord, grant me from Yourself a good offspring. Indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication."} {So the angels called him while he was standing in prayer in the sanctuary: "Indeed, Allah gives you good tidings of Yahya, confirming a word from Allah"}; its name, that is, the word from Allah, is Isa son of Maryam. Thus the glad tidings of this noble prophet included the glad tidings of Isa son of Maryam, and the confirmation of him and the testimony to his messengership. This word from Allah is a noble word which Allah specially attributed to Isa son of Maryam; otherwise it is among His words by which He brought creation into being, as He said: {Indeed, the example of Isa with Allah is like that of Adam; He created him from dust, then said to him, "Be," and he is.}

As for His saying: {and a master (sayyid) and chaste (hasur)}; that is, this one given good tidings, Yahya, is a master among the excellent and honoured messengers. As for al-hasur, it has been said that he is one who cannot father children and has no desire for women, and it has been said that he is one who was preserved and protected from sins and harmful desires; and this latter is the more fitting of the two meanings. {And a prophet from among the righteous}; those who have reached the lofty summit of righteousness. {He said: "My Lord, how will I have a boy when old age has already reached me and my wife is barren?"}; these are two obstacles, so by what means, O Lord, will this be achieved given what contradicts it? {He said: "Thus Allah does what He wills."}; for just as His wisdom requires that affairs proceed by their well-known causes, He may also break such patterns, for He is the Doer of what He wills, to whose power the causes are subservient and into whose will and determination they are subject, so nothing among causes resists His power, however strong they may be. {He said: "My Lord, make for me a sign."}; so that joy and glad expectation may arise, even though, O Lord, he was certain of what he had been told; but the soul rejoices, and the heart finds rest in the preliminaries of mercy and kindness. {He said: "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gesture."} During this period {remember your Lord much and glorify Him in the evening and the morning}; at the beginning and end of the day. So he was prevented from speaking during this period. In this there was a fitting sign for the birth of a child from an aged man and a barren wife, and his inability to address people while his tongue was active with the remembrance and glorification of Allah was another sign. Then joy and gladness came to him, and he thanked Allah and increased in remembrance and glorification in the evenings and mornings.

This child was among the blessings of Maryam bint 'Imran upon Zakariya, for what Allah had bestowed upon her of that provision, which came without account, reminded him and stirred him to humble supplication and asking. Allah, exalted is He, is the One who bestows favour through both the cause and the effect, but He decrees desirable matters at the hands of one whom He loves, so that Allah may raise his rank and magnify his reward.

Then Allah, exalted is He, returned to the mention of Maryam, and that she had reached a great degree of worship and perfection. He said: {And when the angels said, "O Maryam, indeed Allah has chosen you"}; that is, selected you and bestowed upon you noble attributes and beautiful character {and purified you}; from base character {and chosen you above the women of the worlds}. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Many men have reached perfection, but among women none reached perfection except Maryam bint 'Imran, Asiya bint Muzahim, and Khadijah bint Khuwaylid; and the excellence of 'A'isha over women is like the excellence of tharid over other food." Then the angels called to her by Allah's command, so that she might rejoice in the blessings of Allah, give thanks to Allah, fulfil His rights, and occupy herself in His service. For this reason the angels said: {"O Maryam, be devoutly obedient to your Lord and prostrate and bow with those who bow."}; that is, increase in obedience, humility and submission to your Lord, and maintain that continually; {and bow with those who bow}; that is, pray with those who pray. So she performed all that she was commanded, and she excelled and surpassed in her perfection.

Since this story and others are among the greatest proofs of the messengership of Muhammad (ﷺ), in that he related them in detail, verified, without addition or deficiency, and this could only be because it is a revelation from the Mighty, the Wise, and not learned from people, Allah said: {That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you, and you were not with them when they cast their pens, [to see] which of them would undertake the guardianship of Maryam}; when her mother brought her, they disputed as to which of them would be her guardian, since she was the daughter of their leader and chief, and each of them desired good and reward from Allah, until the dispute reached the point where they drew lots over her, casting their pens and drawing lots, and the lot fell upon Zakariya, as a mercy from Allah to him and to her.

So you, O Messenger, were not present at that situation so as to know it and relate it to the people; rather, Allah informed you of it. And this is the greatest purpose of relating stories: that lessons be drawn from them, and the greatest lessons and proofs derived from them concern monotheism, messengership, resurrection and other great foundations. {When the angels said, "O Maryam, indeed Allah gives you good tidings of a word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, Isa son of Maryam, distinguished in this world and the Hereafter and among those brought near."}; that is, he has eminence and great standing in this world and the Hereafter in the sight of creation, and along with that he is, in the sight of Allah, among those brought near, who are the closest of creation to Allah and the highest in rank. This is a glad tiding unlike any other glad tiding. And among the completeness of this glad tiding is that {he will speak to the people in the cradle}; so his speech will be a sign from the signs of Allah and a mercy from Him to his mother and to the creation. Likewise, {and in maturity}; that is, in the state of his middle age, and this is speech of prophethood, call and guidance. His speech in the cradle contains signs and proofs of his truthfulness and prophethood and of the innocence of his mother from the evil suspicions that might be cast upon her; his speech in maturity contains his great benefit to creation and his being an intermediary between them and their Lord in His revelation and the conveying of His religion and law. Along with that, he is {among the righteous}; those whom Allah has made upright in heart through knowledge and love of Him, in tongue through praise and remembrance of Him, and in limbs through obedience and service to Him. {She said: "My Lord, how can I have a child when no man has touched me?"}; and this is one of the strange matters. {He said: "Thus Allah creates what He wills."}; so that the servants may know that He is capable of all things and that nothing can impede His will. {When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.} {And He will teach him the Book}; that is, the genus of previous scriptures and judgment among people; and He will give him prophethood and make him {a messenger to the Children of Israel}; and He will support him with clear signs and overwhelming proofs, as He said: {"Indeed, I have come to you with a sign from your Lord"}; which shows you that I am truly the messenger of Allah. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 3, verse 33–55:

This is among His greatest favours and the finest objects of His generosity and munificence. {And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing}: He knows who deserves virtue and preference, and He places His bounty where His wisdom requires. 

When He established the greatness of these households, He mentioned the story of Maryam and her son Isa (ﷺ), and how the two of them descended from these virtuous households, and how their circumstances shifted from the beginning of their affair to its end. The wife of 'Imran said, humbly supplicating her Lord and drawing near to Him by this act which He loves, which includes the magnification of His House and constant obedience to Him: {Indeed, I have dedicated to You what is in my womb, consecrated (muharraran)}; that is, a servant to the house of worship, filled with those who worship. {So accept it from me}; that is, make this deed founded upon faith and sincerity, bearing fruit of good and reward. {Indeed, You are the All-Hearing, All-Knowing.} {So when she delivered her, she said, "My Lord, I have delivered a female," and Allah was most knowing of what she delivered, "and the male is not like the female."}

It was as if in this statement there was a kind of humble supplication and brokenness of soul, since her vow had been based on the expectation that the child would be a male, who would possess the strength, service, and capacity for this task that people of strength possess, whereas a female is different in this regard. So Allah consoled her heart and accepted her vow, and this female became more perfect and complete than many males, indeed than most of them, and greater objectives were attained through her than through a male. Therefore He said: {So her Lord accepted her with good acceptance and caused her to grow in a good growth}; that is, she was raised with a wondrous upbringing—religious, moral, and cultured—through which her circumstances were perfected, her words and deeds were made righteous, and her perfection flourished. Allah facilitated for her Zakariya as guardian, and this is among Allah's favours upon a servant: that He makes whoever takes charge of his upbringing one of the perfected and reforming.

Then Allah honoured Maryam and Zakariya, in that He made easy for Maryam a provision that came without toil or hardship, and it was purely a dignity with which Allah honoured her, since {whenever Zakariya entered upon her the sanctuary (mihrab)}, which is the place of worship, and this indicates her frequent prayer and constant presence in her sanctuary, {he found with her provision}, ready and prepared. He said: {"From where is this for you?" She said, "It is from Allah. It was as if in this statement there was a kind of humble supplication and brokenness of soul, since her vow had been based on the expectation that the child would be a male, who would possess the strength, service, and capacity for this task that people of strength possess, whereas a female is different in this regard. So Allah consoled her heart and accepted her vow, and this female became more perfect and complete than many males, indeed than most of them, and greater objectives were attained through her than through a male. Therefore He said: {So her Lord accepted her with good acceptance and caused her to grow in a good growth}; that is, she was raised with a wondrous upbringing—religious, moral, and cultured—through which her circumstances were perfected, her words and deeds were made righteous, and her perfection flourished. Allah facilitated for her Zakariya as guardian, and this is among Allah's favours upon a servant: that He makes whoever takes charge of his upbringing one of the perfected and reforming.

He said: {"From where is this for you?" She said, "It is from Allah. Then joy and gladness came to him, and he thanked Allah and increased in remembrance and glorification in the evenings and mornings.

Thus it is known that he is the messenger of Allah and that what he brought is truth without doubt. Also, His saying: {and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you}; that is, to lighten for you some of the burdens and shackles. {So fear Allah and obey me. Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him.} This is what all the messengers called to: worshipping Allah alone without partner and obeying them. This is the straight path which whoever follows leads him to the Gardens of Bliss.

{33–55} Allah, exalted is He, has among His servants chosen ones (asfiya'), whom He selects, chooses, and bestows upon with lofty virtues, sublime attributes, beneficial knowledge, righteous deeds, and diverse distinctions. He mentioned these great households and what they contained of perfected men (kummal al-rijal) who attained the qualities of perfection, and that virtue and goodness continued in their offspring, encompassing both their males and their females. This is among His greatest favours and the finest objects of His generosity and munificence. {And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing}: He knows who deserves virtue and preference, and He places His bounty where His wisdom requires. 

When He established the greatness of these households, He mentioned the story of Maryam and her son Isa (ﷺ), and how the two of them descended from these virtuous households, and how their circumstances shifted from the beginning of their affair to its end. The wife of 'Imran said, humbly supplicating her Lord and drawing near to Him by this act which He loves, which includes the magnification of His House and constant obedience to Him: {Indeed, I have dedicated to You what is in my womb, consecrated (muharraran)}; that is, a servant to the house of worship, filled with those who worship. {So accept it from me}; that is, make this deed founded upon faith and sincerity, bearing fruit of good and reward. {Indeed, You are the All-Hearing, All-Knowing.} {So when she delivered her, she said, "My Lord, I have delivered a female," and Allah was most knowing of what she delivered, "and the male is not like the female."}

It was as if in this statement there was a kind of humble supplication and brokenness of soul, since her vow had been based on the expectation that the child would be a male, who would possess the strength, service, and capacity for this task that people of strength possess, whereas a female is different in this regard. So Allah consoled her heart and accepted her vow, and this female became more perfect and complete than many males, indeed than most of them, and greater objectives were attained through her than through a male. Therefore He said: {So her Lord accepted her with good acceptance and caused her to grow in a good growth}; that is, she was raised with a wondrous upbringing—religious, moral, and cultured—through which her circumstances were perfected, her words and deeds were made righteous, and her perfection flourished. Allah facilitated for her Zakariya as guardian, and this is among Allah's favours upon a servant: that He makes whoever takes charge of his upbringing one of the perfected and reforming.

Then Allah honoured Maryam and Zakariya, in that He made easy for Maryam a provision that came without toil or hardship, and it was purely a dignity with which Allah honoured her, since {whenever Zakariya entered upon her the sanctuary (mihrab)}, which is the place of worship, and this indicates her frequent prayer and constant presence in her sanctuary, {he found with her provision}, ready and prepared. He said: {"From where is this for you?" She said, "It is from Allah. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without account."} When Zakariya saw this state and the righteousness and kindness of Allah toward her, it reminded him to ask Allah for a child in a time of despair regarding it, so he said: {"My Lord, grant me from Yourself a good offspring. Indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication."} {So the angels called him while he was standing in prayer in the sanctuary: "Indeed, Allah gives you good tidings of Yahya, confirming a word from Allah"}; its name, that is, the word from Allah, is Isa son of Maryam. Thus the glad tidings of this noble prophet included the glad tidings of Isa son of Maryam, and the confirmation of him and the testimony to his messengership. This word from Allah is a noble word which Allah specially attributed to Isa son of Maryam; otherwise it is among His words by which He brought creation into being, as He said: {Indeed, the example of Isa with Allah is like that of Adam; He created him from dust, then said to him, "Be," and he is.}

As for His saying: {and a master (sayyid) and chaste (hasur)}; that is, this one given good tidings, Yahya, is a master among the excellent and honoured messengers. As for al-hasur, it has been said that he is one who cannot father children and has no desire for women, and it has been said that he is one who was preserved and protected from sins and harmful desires; and this latter is the more fitting of the two meanings. {And a prophet from among the righteous}; those who have reached the lofty summit of righteousness. {He said: "My Lord, how will I have a boy when old age has already reached me and my wife is barren?"}; these are two obstacles, so by what means, O Lord, will this be achieved given what contradicts it? {He said: "Thus Allah does what He wills."}; for just as His wisdom requires that affairs proceed by their well-known causes, He may also break such patterns, for He is the Doer of what He wills, to whose power the causes are subservient and into whose will and determination they are subject, so nothing among causes resists His power, however strong they may be. {He said: "My Lord, make for me a sign."}; so that joy and glad expectation may arise, even though, O Lord, he was certain of what he had been told; but the soul rejoices, and the heart finds rest in the preliminaries of mercy and kindness. {He said: "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gesture."} During this period {remember your Lord much and glorify Him in the evening and the morning}; at the beginning and end of the day. So he was prevented from speaking during this period. In this there was a fitting sign for the birth of a child from an aged man and a barren wife, and his inability to address people while his tongue was active with the remembrance and glorification of Allah was another sign. Then joy and gladness came to him, and he thanked Allah and increased in remembrance and glorification in the evenings and mornings.

This child was among the blessings of Maryam bint 'Imran upon Zakariya, for what Allah had bestowed upon her of that provision, which came without account, reminded him and stirred him to humble supplication and asking. Allah, exalted is He, is the One who bestows favour through both the cause and the effect, but He decrees desirable matters at the hands of one whom He loves, so that Allah may raise his rank and magnify his reward.

Then Allah, exalted is He, returned to the mention of Maryam, and that she had reached a great degree of worship and perfection. He said: {And when the angels said, "O Maryam, indeed Allah has chosen you"}; that is, selected you and bestowed upon you noble attributes and beautiful character {and purified you}; from base character {and chosen you above the women of the worlds}. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Many men have reached perfection, but among women none reached perfection except Maryam bint 'Imran, Asiya bint Muzahim, and Khadijah bint Khuwaylid; and the excellence of 'A'isha over women is like the excellence of tharid over other food." Then the angels called to her by Allah's command, so that she might rejoice in the blessings of Allah, give thanks to Allah, fulfil His rights, and occupy herself in His service. For this reason the angels said: {"O Maryam, be devoutly obedient to your Lord and prostrate and bow with those who bow."}; that is, increase in obedience, humility and submission to your Lord, and maintain that continually; {and bow with those who bow}; that is, pray with those who pray. So she performed all that she was commanded, and she excelled and surpassed in her perfection.

Since this story and others are among the greatest proofs of the messengership of Muhammad (ﷺ), in that he related them in detail, verified, without addition or deficiency, and this could only be because it is a revelation from the Mighty, the Wise, and not learned from people, Allah said: {That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you, and you were not with them when they cast their pens, [to see] which of them would undertake the guardianship of Maryam}; when her mother brought her, they disputed as to which of them would be her guardian, since she was the daughter of their leader and chief, and each of them desired good and reward from Allah, until the dispute reached the point where they drew lots over her, casting their pens and drawing lots, and the lot fell upon Zakariya, as a mercy from Allah to him and to her.

So you, O Messenger, were not present at that situation so as to know it and relate it to the people; rather, Allah informed you of it. And this is the greatest purpose of relating stories: that lessons be drawn from them, and the greatest lessons and proofs derived from them concern monotheism, messengership, resurrection and other great foundations. {When the angels said, "O Maryam, indeed Allah gives you good tidings of a word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, Isa son of Maryam, distinguished in this world and the Hereafter and among those brought near."}; that is, he has eminence and great standing in this world and the Hereafter in the sight of creation, and along with that he is, in the sight of Allah, among those brought near, who are the closest of creation to Allah and the highest in rank. This is a glad tiding unlike any other glad tiding. And among the completeness of this glad tiding is that {he will speak to the people in the cradle}; so his speech will be a sign from the signs of Allah and a mercy from Him to his mother and to the creation. Likewise, {and in maturity}; that is, in the state of his middle age, and this is speech of prophethood, call and guidance. His speech in the cradle contains signs and proofs of his truthfulness and prophethood and of the innocence of his mother from the evil suspicions that might be cast upon her; his speech in maturity contains his great benefit to creation and his being an intermediary between them and their Lord in His revelation and the conveying of His religion and law. Along with that, he is {among the righteous}; those whom Allah has made upright in heart through knowledge and love of Him, in tongue through praise and remembrance of Him, and in limbs through obedience and service to Him. {She said: "My Lord, how can I have a child when no man has touched me?"}; and this is one of the strange matters. {He said: "Thus Allah creates what He wills."}; so that the servants may know that He is capable of all things and that nothing can impede His will. {When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.} {And He will teach him the Book}; that is, the genus of previous scriptures and judgment among people; and He will give him prophethood and make him {a messenger to the Children of Israel}; and He will support him with clear signs and overwhelming proofs, as He said: {"Indeed, I have come to you with a sign from your Lord"}; which shows you that I am truly the messenger of Allah. That sign is: {"Indeed, I will create for you from clay like the form of a bird, then breathe into it and it will be a bird by the permission of Allah. And I will heal the one born blind and the leper, and I will give life to the dead by the permission of Allah. And I will inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses. Indeed, in that}; the aforementioned {is a sign for you if you are believers."} {And confirming what came before me of the Torah}; so Allah supported him with two kinds of signs and proofs, extraordinary and strange, which none other than prophets can produce, and with the messengership, the call and the religion he brought, namely that it is the religion of the Torah and the religion of the earlier prophets. This is the greatest proof of the truthfulness of the truthful, for had he been among the liars, he would have contradicted what the messengers brought and opposed them in their fundamentals and their branches. Thus it is known that he is the messenger of Allah and that what he brought is truth without doubt. Also, His saying: {and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you}; that is, to lighten for you some of the burdens and shackles. {So fear Allah and obey me. Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him.} This is what all the messengers called to: worshipping Allah alone without partner and obeying them. This is the straight path which whoever follows leads him to the Gardens of Bliss.

Then the factions of the Children of Israel differed concerning Isa. Some of them believed in him and followed him, and some disbelieved in him, denied him, and accused his mother of immorality, like the Jews. {So when Isa perceived disbelief from them}; and the consensus to reject his call {he said}; calling upon the Children of Israel to support him: {"Who will be my helpers for Allah?" The disciples (hawariyyun) said}; that is, the helpers: {"We are the helpers of Allah. We believe in Allah, and bear witness that we are Muslims."} This is among the favours of Allah upon them and upon Isa, in that He inspired these disciples with faith in him, submission to his obedience, and support for his messenger. {"Our Lord, we believe in what You have sent down and have followed the messenger, so register us among the witnesses."}; this is a complete commitment to faith in all that Allah sent down and to obedience to His messenger; {so register us among the witnesses}; to You for Your oneness, and to Your prophet for his messengership, and to Your religion for its truth and sincerity. As for those from whom Isa perceived disbelief, who were the majority of the Children of Israel, {they schemed}; against Isa, {and Allah schemed}; against them, {and Allah is the best of schemers}; so they agreed to kill him and crucify him. Their likeness was made to appear to them as that of Isa, so they seized the one who had been made to resemble him. Allah said to Isa: {"Indeed, I will cause you to die and raise you to Myself and purify you from those who disbelieve."} So Allah raised him to Himself, purified him from those who disbelieved, and those who killed him were crucified, thinking that he was Isa, and they earned a great sin.

Isa son of Maryam will descend at the end of this Ummah as a just judge, who will kill the swine, break the cross, and follow what Muhammad (ﷺ) brought, and the liars will know their delusion and deception, and that they are deluded and deceived. As for His saying: {and I will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection}; what is meant by those who followed him is the group that believed in him, whom Allah supported against those who deviated from his religion. Then when the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ) came, they were truly his followers, so Allah strengthened them and gave them victory over all the disbelievers, and made them prevail with the religion that Muhammad (ﷺ) brought them. {Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely grant them succession upon the earth}; the verse continues. But Allah's wisdom is just, for it requires that whoever adheres to the religion is granted clear victory, and that whoever abandons His command and prohibition, rejects His law and dares to commit His sins, will be punished and have enemies set over him. And Allah is Mighty and Wise. His saying: {Then to Me is your return, and I will judge between you concerning that over which you used to differ.}

Thus it is known that he is the messenger of Allah and that what he brought is truth without doubt. Also, His saying: {and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you}; that is, to lighten for you some of the burdens and shackles. {So fear Allah and obey me. This is the straight path which whoever follows leads him to the Gardens of Bliss.

Then the factions of the Children of Israel differed concerning Isa. Some of them believed in him and followed him, and some disbelieved in him, denied him, and accused his mother of immorality, like the Jews. {So when Isa perceived disbelief from them}; and the consensus to reject his call {he said}; calling upon the Children of Israel to support him: {"Who will be my helpers for Allah?" This is among His greatest favours and the finest objects of His generosity and munificence. {And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing}: He knows who deserves virtue and preference, and He places His bounty where His wisdom requires.

It was as if in this statement there was a kind of humble supplication and brokenness of soul, since her vow had been based on the expectation that the child would be a male, who would possess the strength, service, and capacity for this task that people of strength possess, whereas a female is different in this regard. So Allah consoled her heart and accepted her vow, and this female became more perfect and complete than many males, indeed than most of them, and greater objectives were attained through her than through a male. Therefore He said: {So her Lord accepted her with good acceptance and caused her to grow in a good growth}; that is, she was raised with a wondrous upbringing—religious, moral, and cultured—through which her circumstances were perfected, her words and deeds were made righteous, and her perfection flourished. He said: {"From where is this for you?" She said, "It is from Allah. It was as if in this statement there was a kind of humble supplication and brokenness of soul, since her vow had been based on the expectation that the child would be a male, who would possess the strength, service, and capacity for this task that people of strength possess, whereas a female is different in this regard. So Allah consoled her heart and accepted her vow, and this female became more perfect and complete than many males, indeed than most of them, and greater objectives were attained through her than through a male. Therefore He said: {So her Lord accepted her with good acceptance and caused her to grow in a good growth}; that is, she was raised with a wondrous upbringing—religious, moral, and cultured—through which her circumstances were perfected, her words and deeds were made righteous, and her perfection flourished. Allah facilitated for her Zakariya as guardian, and this is among Allah's favours upon a servant: that He makes whoever takes charge of his upbringing one of the perfected and reforming.

He said: {"From where is this for you?" She said, "It is from Allah. Then joy and gladness came to him, and he thanked Allah and increased in remembrance and glorification in the evenings and mornings.

Thus it is known that he is the messenger of Allah and that what he brought is truth without doubt. Also, His saying: {and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you}; that is, to lighten for you some of the burdens and shackles. {So fear Allah and obey me. Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him.} This is what all the messengers called to: worshipping Allah alone without partner and obeying them. This is the straight path which whoever follows leads him to the Gardens of Bliss.

{33–55} Allah, exalted is He, has among His servants chosen ones (asfiya'), whom He selects, chooses, and bestows upon with lofty virtues, sublime attributes, beneficial knowledge, righteous deeds, and diverse distinctions. He mentioned these great households and what they contained of perfected men (kummal al-rijal) who attained the qualities of perfection, and that virtue and goodness continued in their offspring, encompassing both their males and their females. This is among His greatest favours and the finest objects of His generosity and munificence. {And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing}: He knows who deserves virtue and preference, and He places His bounty where His wisdom requires. 

When He established the greatness of these households, He mentioned the story of Maryam and her son Isa (ﷺ), and how the two of them descended from these virtuous households, and how their circumstances shifted from the beginning of their affair to its end. The wife of 'Imran said, humbly supplicating her Lord and drawing near to Him by this act which He loves, which includes the magnification of His House and constant obedience to Him: {Indeed, I have dedicated to You what is in my womb, consecrated (muharraran)}; that is, a servant to the house of worship, filled with those who worship. {So accept it from me}; that is, make this deed founded upon faith and sincerity, bearing fruit of good and reward. {Indeed, You are the All-Hearing, All-Knowing.} {So when she delivered her, she said, "My Lord, I have delivered a female," and Allah was most knowing of what she delivered, "and the male is not like the female."}

It was as if in this statement there was a kind of humble supplication and brokenness of soul, since her vow had been based on the expectation that the child would be a male, who would possess the strength, service, and capacity for this task that people of strength possess, whereas a female is different in this regard. So Allah consoled her heart and accepted her vow, and this female became more perfect and complete than many males, indeed than most of them, and greater objectives were attained through her than through a male. Therefore He said: {So her Lord accepted her with good acceptance and caused her to grow in a good growth}; that is, she was raised with a wondrous upbringing—religious, moral, and cultured—through which her circumstances were perfected, her words and deeds were made righteous, and her perfection flourished. Allah facilitated for her Zakariya as guardian, and this is among Allah's favours upon a servant: that He makes whoever takes charge of his upbringing one of the perfected and reforming.

Then Allah honoured Maryam and Zakariya, in that He made easy for Maryam a provision that came without toil or hardship, and it was purely a dignity with which Allah honoured her, since {whenever Zakariya entered upon her the sanctuary (mihrab)}, which is the place of worship, and this indicates her frequent prayer and constant presence in her sanctuary, {he found with her provision}, ready and prepared. He said: {"From where is this for you?" She said, "It is from Allah. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without account."} When Zakariya saw this state and the righteousness and kindness of Allah toward her, it reminded him to ask Allah for a child in a time of despair regarding it, so he said: {"My Lord, grant me from Yourself a good offspring. Indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication."} {So the angels called him while he was standing in prayer in the sanctuary: "Indeed, Allah gives you good tidings of Yahya, confirming a word from Allah"}; its name, that is, the word from Allah, is Isa son of Maryam. Thus the glad tidings of this noble prophet included the glad tidings of Isa son of Maryam, and the confirmation of him and the testimony to his messengership. This word from Allah is a noble word which Allah specially attributed to Isa son of Maryam; otherwise it is among His words by which He brought creation into being, as He said: {Indeed, the example of Isa with Allah is like that of Adam; He created him from dust, then said to him, "Be," and he is.}

As for His saying: {and a master (sayyid) and chaste (hasur)}; that is, this one given good tidings, Yahya, is a master among the excellent and honoured messengers. As for al-hasur, it has been said that he is one who cannot father children and has no desire for women, and it has been said that he is one who was preserved and protected from sins and harmful desires; and this latter is the more fitting of the two meanings. {And a prophet from among the righteous}; those who have reached the lofty summit of righteousness. {He said: "My Lord, how will I have a boy when old age has already reached me and my wife is barren?"}; these are two obstacles, so by what means, O Lord, will this be achieved given what contradicts it? {He said: "Thus Allah does what He wills."}; for just as His wisdom requires that affairs proceed by their well-known causes, He may also break such patterns, for He is the Doer of what He wills, to whose power the causes are subservient and into whose will and determination they are subject, so nothing among causes resists His power, however strong they may be. {He said: "My Lord, make for me a sign."}; so that joy and glad expectation may arise, even though, O Lord, he was certain of what he had been told; but the soul rejoices, and the heart finds rest in the preliminaries of mercy and kindness. {He said: "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gesture."} During this period {remember your Lord much and glorify Him in the evening and the morning}; at the beginning and end of the day. So he was prevented from speaking during this period. In this there was a fitting sign for the birth of a child from an aged man and a barren wife, and his inability to address people while his tongue was active with the remembrance and glorification of Allah was another sign. Then joy and gladness came to him, and he thanked Allah and increased in remembrance and glorification in the evenings and mornings.

This child was among the blessings of Maryam bint 'Imran upon Zakariya, for what Allah had bestowed upon her of that provision, which came without account, reminded him and stirred him to humble supplication and asking. Allah, exalted is He, is the One who bestows favour through both the cause and the effect, but He decrees desirable matters at the hands of one whom He loves, so that Allah may raise his rank and magnify his reward.

Then Allah, exalted is He, returned to the mention of Maryam, and that she had reached a great degree of worship and perfection. He said: {And when the angels said, "O Maryam, indeed Allah has chosen you"}; that is, selected you and bestowed upon you noble attributes and beautiful character {and purified you}; from base character {and chosen you above the women of the worlds}. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Many men have reached perfection, but among women none reached perfection except Maryam bint 'Imran, Asiya bint Muzahim, and Khadijah bint Khuwaylid; and the excellence of 'A'isha over women is like the excellence of tharid over other food." Then the angels called to her by Allah's command, so that she might rejoice in the blessings of Allah, give thanks to Allah, fulfil His rights, and occupy herself in His service. For this reason the angels said: {"O Maryam, be devoutly obedient to your Lord and prostrate and bow with those who bow."}; that is, increase in obedience, humility and submission to your Lord, and maintain that continually; {and bow with those who bow}; that is, pray with those who pray. So she performed all that she was commanded, and she excelled and surpassed in her perfection.

Since this story and others are among the greatest proofs of the messengership of Muhammad (ﷺ), in that he related them in detail, verified, without addition or deficiency, and this could only be because it is a revelation from the Mighty, the Wise, and not learned from people, Allah said: {That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you, and you were not with them when they cast their pens, [to see] which of them would undertake the guardianship of Maryam}; when her mother brought her, they disputed as to which of them would be her guardian, since she was the daughter of their leader and chief, and each of them desired good and reward from Allah, until the dispute reached the point where they drew lots over her, casting their pens and drawing lots, and the lot fell upon Zakariya, as a mercy from Allah to him and to her.

So you, O Messenger, were not present at that situation so as to know it and relate it to the people; rather, Allah informed you of it. And this is the greatest purpose of relating stories: that lessons be drawn from them, and the greatest lessons and proofs derived from them concern monotheism, messengership, resurrection and other great foundations. {When the angels said, "O Maryam, indeed Allah gives you good tidings of a word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, Isa son of Maryam, distinguished in this world and the Hereafter and among those brought near."}; that is, he has eminence and great standing in this world and the Hereafter in the sight of creation, and along with that he is, in the sight of Allah, among those brought near, who are the closest of creation to Allah and the highest in rank. This is a glad tiding unlike any other glad tiding. And among the completeness of this glad tiding is that {he will speak to the people in the cradle}; so his speech will be a sign from the signs of Allah and a mercy from Him to his mother and to the creation. Likewise, {and in maturity}; that is, in the state of his middle age, and this is speech of prophethood, call and guidance. His speech in the cradle contains signs and proofs of his truthfulness and prophethood and of the innocence of his mother from the evil suspicions that might be cast upon her; his speech in maturity contains his great benefit to creation and his being an intermediary between them and their Lord in His revelation and the conveying of His religion and law. Along with that, he is {among the righteous}; those whom Allah has made upright in heart through knowledge and love of Him, in tongue through praise and remembrance of Him, and in limbs through obedience and service to Him. {She said: "My Lord, how can I have a child when no man has touched me?"}; and this is one of the strange matters. {He said: "Thus Allah creates what He wills."}; so that the servants may know that He is capable of all things and that nothing can impede His will. {When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.} {And He will teach him the Book}; that is, the genus of previous scriptures and judgment among people; and He will give him prophethood and make him {a messenger to the Children of Israel}; and He will support him with clear signs and overwhelming proofs, as He said: {"Indeed, I have come to you with a sign from your Lord"}; which shows you that I am truly the messenger of Allah. That sign is: {"Indeed, I will create for you from clay like the form of a bird, then breathe into it and it will be a bird by the permission of Allah. And I will heal the one born blind and the leper, and I will give life to the dead by the permission of Allah. And I will inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses. Indeed, in that}; the aforementioned {is a sign for you if you are believers."} {And confirming what came before me of the Torah}; so Allah supported him with two kinds of signs and proofs, extraordinary and strange, which none other than prophets can produce, and with the messengership, the call and the religion he brought, namely that it is the religion of the Torah and the religion of the earlier prophets. This is the greatest proof of the truthfulness of the truthful, for had he been among the liars, he would have contradicted what the messengers brought and opposed them in their fundamentals and their branches. Thus it is known that he is the messenger of Allah and that what he brought is truth without doubt. Also, His saying: {and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you}; that is, to lighten for you some of the burdens and shackles. {So fear Allah and obey me. Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him.} This is what all the messengers called to: worshipping Allah alone without partner and obeying them. This is the straight path which whoever follows leads him to the Gardens of Bliss.

Then the factions of the Children of Israel differed concerning Isa. Some of them believed in him and followed him, and some disbelieved in him, denied him, and accused his mother of immorality, like the Jews. {So when Isa perceived disbelief from them}; and the consensus to reject his call {he said}; calling upon the Children of Israel to support him: {"Who will be my helpers for Allah?" The disciples (hawariyyun) said}; that is, the helpers: {"We are the helpers of Allah. We believe in Allah, and bear witness that we are Muslims."} This is among the favours of Allah upon them and upon Isa, in that He inspired these disciples with faith in him, submission to his obedience, and support for his messenger. {"Our Lord, we believe in what You have sent down and have followed the messenger, so register us among the witnesses."}; this is a complete commitment to faith in all that Allah sent down and to obedience to His messenger; {so register us among the witnesses}; to You for Your oneness, and to Your prophet for his messengership, and to Your religion for its truth and sincerity. As for those from whom Isa perceived disbelief, who were the majority of the Children of Israel, {they schemed}; against Isa, {and Allah schemed}; against them, {and Allah is the best of schemers}; so they agreed to kill him and crucify him. Their likeness was made to appear to them as that of Isa, so they seized the one who had been made to resemble him. Allah said to Isa: {"Indeed, I will cause you to die and raise you to Myself and purify you from those who disbelieve."} So Allah raised him to Himself, purified him from those who disbelieved, and those who killed him were crucified, thinking that he was Isa, and they earned a great sin.

Isa son of Maryam will descend at the end of this Ummah as a just judge, who will kill the swine, break the cross, and follow what Muhammad (ﷺ) brought, and the liars will know their delusion and deception, and that they are deluded and deceived. As for His saying: {and I will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection}; what is meant by those who followed him is the group that believed in him, whom Allah supported against those who deviated from his religion. Then when the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ) came, they were truly his followers, so Allah strengthened them and gave them victory over all the disbelievers, and made them prevail with the religion that Muhammad (ﷺ) brought them. {Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely grant them succession upon the earth}; the verse continues. But Allah's wisdom is just, for it requires that whoever adheres to the religion is granted clear victory, and that whoever abandons His command and prohibition, rejects His law and dares to commit His sins, will be punished and have enemies set over him. And Allah is Mighty and Wise. His saying: {Then to Me is your return, and I will judge between you concerning that over which you used to differ.}

Thus it is known that he is the messenger of Allah and that what he brought is truth without doubt. Also, His saying: {and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you}; that is, to lighten for you some of the burdens and shackles. {So fear Allah and obey me. This is the straight path which whoever follows leads him to the Gardens of Bliss.

Then the factions of the Children of Israel differed concerning Isa. Some of them believed in him and followed him, and some disbelieved in him, denied him, and accused his mother of immorality, like the Jews. {So when Isa perceived disbelief from them}; and the consensus to reject his call {he said}; calling upon the Children of Israel to support him: {"Who will be my helpers for Allah?"
