In this there was a fitting sign for the birth of a child from an aged man and a barren wife, and his inability to address people while his tongue was active with the remembrance and glorification of Allah was another sign. Then joy and gladness came to him, and he thanked Allah and increased in remembrance and glorification in the evenings and mornings.

This child was among the blessings of Maryam bint 'Imran upon Zakariya, for what Allah had bestowed upon her of that provision, which came without account, reminded him and stirred him to humble supplication and asking. Allah, exalted is He, is the One who bestows favour through both the cause and the effect, but He decrees desirable matters at the hands of one whom He loves, so that Allah may raise his rank and magnify his reward.

Then Allah, exalted is He, returned to the mention of Maryam, and that she had reached a great degree of worship and perfection. He said: {And when the angels said, "O Maryam, indeed Allah has chosen you"}; that is, selected you and bestowed upon you noble attributes and beautiful character {and purified you}; from base character {and chosen you above the women of the worlds}. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Many men have reached perfection, but among women none reached perfection except Maryam bint 'Imran, Asiya bint Muzahim, and Khadijah bint Khuwaylid; and the excellence of 'A'isha over women is like the excellence of tharid over other food." Then the angels called to her by Allah's command, so that she might rejoice in the blessings of Allah, give thanks to Allah, fulfil His rights, and occupy herself in His service. For this reason the angels said: {"O Maryam, be devoutly obedient to your Lord and prostrate and bow with those who bow."}; that is, increase in obedience, humility and submission to your Lord, and maintain that continually; {and bow with those who bow}; that is, pray with those who pray. So she performed all that she was commanded, and she excelled and surpassed in her perfection.

Since this story and others are among the greatest proofs of the messengership of Muhammad (ﷺ), in that he related them in detail, verified, without addition or deficiency, and this could only be because it is a revelation from the Mighty, the Wise, and not learned from people, Allah said: {That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you, and you were not with them when they cast their pens, [to see] which of them would undertake the guardianship of Maryam}; when her mother brought her, they disputed as to which of them would be her guardian, since she was the daughter of their leader and chief, and each of them desired good and reward from Allah, until the dispute reached the point where they drew lots over her, casting their pens and drawing lots, and the lot fell upon Zakariya, as a mercy from Allah to him and to her.

So you, O Messenger, were not present at that situation so as to know it and relate it to the people; rather, Allah informed you of it. And this is the greatest purpose of relating stories: that lessons be drawn from them, and the greatest lessons and proofs derived from them concern monotheism, messengership, resurrection and other great foundations. {When the angels said, "O Maryam, indeed Allah gives you good tidings of a word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, Isa son of Maryam, distinguished in this world and the Hereafter and among those brought near."}; that is, he has eminence and great standing in this world and the Hereafter in the sight of creation, and along with that he is, in the sight of Allah, among those brought near, who are the closest of creation to Allah and the highest in rank. This is a glad tiding unlike any other glad tiding. And among the completeness of this glad tiding is that {he will speak to the people in the cradle}; so his speech will be a sign from the signs of Allah and a mercy from Him to his mother and to the creation. Likewise, {and in maturity}; that is, in the state of his middle age, and this is speech of prophethood, call and guidance. His speech in the cradle contains signs and proofs of his truthfulness and prophethood and of the innocence of his mother from the evil suspicions that might be cast upon her; his speech in maturity contains his great benefit to creation and his being an intermediary between them and their Lord in His revelation and the conveying of His religion and law. Along with that, he is {among the righteous}; those whom Allah has made upright in heart through knowledge and love of Him, in tongue through praise and remembrance of Him, and in limbs through obedience and service to Him. {She said: "My Lord, how can I have a child when no man has touched me?"}; and this is one of the strange matters. {He said: "Thus Allah creates what He wills."}; so that the servants may know that He is capable of all things and that nothing can impede His will. {When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.} {And He will teach him the Book}; that is, the genus of previous scriptures and judgment among people; and He will give him prophethood and make him {a messenger to the Children of Israel}; and He will support him with clear signs and overwhelming proofs, as He said: {"Indeed, I have come to you with a sign from your Lord"}; which shows you that I am truly the messenger of Allah. That sign is: {"Indeed, I will create for you from clay like the form of a bird, then breathe into it and it will be a bird by the permission of Allah. And I will heal the one born blind and the leper, and I will give life to the dead by the permission of Allah. And I will inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses. Indeed, in that}; the aforementioned {is a sign for you if you are believers."} {And confirming what came before me of the Torah}; so Allah supported him with two kinds of signs and proofs, extraordinary and strange, which none other than prophets can produce, and with the messengership, the call and the religion he brought, namely that it is the religion of the Torah and the religion of the earlier prophets. This is the greatest proof of the truthfulness of the truthful, for had he been among the liars, he would have contradicted what the messengers brought and opposed them in their fundamentals and their branches. Thus it is known that he is the messenger of Allah and that what he brought is truth without doubt. Also, His saying: {and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you}; that is, to lighten for you some of the burdens and shackles. {So fear Allah and obey me. Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him.} This is what all the messengers called to: worshipping Allah alone without partner and obeying them. This is the straight path which whoever follows leads him to the Gardens of Bliss.

Then the factions of the Children of Israel differed concerning Isa. Some of them believed in him and followed him, and some disbelieved in him, denied him, and accused his mother of immorality, like the Jews. {So when Isa perceived disbelief from them}; and the consensus to reject his call {he said}; calling upon the Children of Israel to support him: {"Who will be my helpers for Allah?" The disciples (hawariyyun) said}; that is, the helpers: {"We are the helpers of Allah. We believe in Allah, and bear witness that we are Muslims."} This is among the favours of Allah upon them and upon Isa, in that He inspired these disciples with faith in him, submission to his obedience, and support for his messenger. {"Our Lord, we believe in what You have sent down and have followed the messenger, so register us among the witnesses."}; this is a complete commitment to faith in all that Allah sent down and to obedience to His messenger; {so register us among the witnesses}; to You for Your oneness, and to Your prophet for his messengership, and to Your religion for its truth and sincerity. As for those from whom Isa perceived disbelief, who were the majority of the Children of Israel, {they schemed}; against Isa, {and Allah schemed}; against them, {and Allah is the best of schemers}; so they agreed to kill him and crucify him. Their likeness was made to appear to them as that of Isa, so they seized the one who had been made to resemble him. Allah said to Isa: {"Indeed, I will cause you to die and raise you to Myself and purify you from those who disbelieve."} So Allah raised him to Himself, purified him from those who disbelieved, and those who killed him were crucified, thinking that he was Isa, and they earned a great sin.

Isa son of Maryam will descend at the end of this Ummah as a just judge, who will kill the swine, break the cross, and follow what Muhammad (ﷺ) brought, and the liars will know their delusion and deception, and that they are deluded and deceived. As for His saying: {and I will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection}; what is meant by those who followed him is the group that believed in him, whom Allah supported against those who deviated from his religion. Then when the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ) came, they were truly his followers, so Allah strengthened them and gave them victory over all the disbelievers, and made them prevail with the religion that Muhammad (ﷺ) brought them. {Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely grant them succession upon the earth}; the verse continues. But Allah's wisdom is just, for it requires that whoever adheres to the religion is granted clear victory, and that whoever abandons His command and prohibition, rejects His law and dares to commit His sins, will be punished and have enemies set over him. And Allah is Mighty and Wise. His saying: {Then to Me is your return, and I will judge between you concerning that over which you used to differ.}

Then He explained what He will do to them, saying:

This reward is general for everyone who possesses these attributes from all the people of the earlier religions. Then, when the Master of the Messengers and Seal of the Prophets was sent, his message abrogated all the previous messages, and his religion abrogated all the religions. Whoever clings to any religion other than this one becomes among the ruined. And His Exalted saying:

Then, when the Master of the Messengers and Seal of the Prophets was sent, his message abrogated all the previous messages, and his religion abrogated all the religions. Whoever clings to any religion other than this one becomes among the ruined. And His Exalted saying:

{58} That is: this great Qur'an, which contains the news of the earlier and later peoples and of the prophets and messengers, is the clear signs of Allah, and it is the one that reminds the servants of everything they need. It is the Wise, the Perfectly Ordained, true in its reports and excellent in its rulings.

The commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 3, verses 59–63:

{59–62} When He mentioned the story of Maryam and Isa and their true account, and that he is a servant upon whom Allah bestowed favor, and that whoever claims that there is in him any aspect of divinity has lied against Allah, and lied against all His prophets, and lied against Isa (ﷺ). The misconception that presented itself to those who took him as a god is a false misconception. Had it had any valid basis, Adam would have been more deserving of it, for he was created without a mother or a father. Yet all of mankind agreed that he is a servant among the servants of Allah. So the claim of Isa's divinity on the ground that he was created from a mother without a father is among the most baseless of claims. This is the truth beyond doubt: that Isa said of himself, ﴿I said to them nothing except what You commanded me: "Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord."﴾

The delegation of the Christians of Najran had come to the Prophet (ﷺ), and they had become rigid in their falsehood after the Prophet (ﷺ) had presented to them the proofs that Isa is a servant of Allah and His messenger, although they claimed his divinity. The situation reached the point that Allah the Exalted commanded him to invoke a mutual curse upon them (mubahala), for the truth had become clear to them, but their stubbornness and fanaticism prevented them from accepting it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) invited them to mubahala, that he would come with his family and his sons, and they would come with their families and their sons, and then they would invoke Allah the Exalted to send down His punishment and curse upon the liars. They deliberated on whether to accept his invitation, and their opinion agreed not to accept it, because they knew that he was truly the prophet of Allah, and that if they engaged in mubahala they and their children and their families would perish. So they made peace with him and offered him the jizya (poll tax), and requested from him a truce and a settlement. The Prophet (ﷺ) accepted their request and did not burden them, because the purpose had been achieved through the clarity of the truth, and their obstinacy was made evident in that they insisted on refusing mubahala. This proves that they were wrongdoers.

Therefore He the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, this is the true narrative﴾; that is, the one about which there is no doubt. ﴿And indeed, Allah is the Exalted in Might﴾ who subdued all existing things by His power and strength, and before whom the inhabitants of the earth and the heavens submitted. Yet He is ﴿the Wise﴾, who places things in their proper places and assigns them their proper stations.

This verse was one that the Prophet (ﷺ) would write to the kings of the People of the Book. Sometimes he would recite in the first rak'ah of the Dawn Sunnah (sunnah al-fajr, the voluntary prayer before the obligatory dawn prayer) the words ﴿Say: "We believe in God..."﴾, to the end of the verse; and he would recite it in the second rak'ah of the Dawn prayer (sunnah al-subh), because it contains the call to one religion, upon which all the prophets and messengers agreed. It encompasses the tawhid of divinity (tawhid al-uluhiyyah), founded on worshipping God alone, with no partner, and on believing that human beings and all creation are in the stage of humanity, so that none of them deserves any of the attributes of lordship or the descriptions of divinity. If the People of the Book and others submit to this, they have been guided. ﴿But if they turn away, then say: "Bear witness that we are Muslims."﴾ This is like the saying of the Most High: ﴿Say: "O disbelievers..."﴾, to the end of it.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 3, verses 65–68:

{65–68} All the religions—the Jews, the Christians, and the polytheists—and likewise all the Muslims, used to claim that they were upon the millah (religious community) of Ibrahim (Abraham). So Allah Most High informed that the people most worthy of him are Muhammad (ﷺ), his followers, and the followers of the Khalil (the Friend, i.e., Ibrahim) before Muhammad (ﷺ). As for the Jews, the Christians, and the polytheists, Ibrahim is free of them and of their allegiance, because his religion is the hanifiyyah (pure monotheism) that is tolerant and easy, in which is faith in all the messengers and all the books. This is the distinguishing feature of the Muslims. As for the claim of the Jews and the Christians that they are upon the millah of Ibrahim, it is known that the Judaism and Christianity that they claim to follow were not established until after the Khalil. How, then, do they argue about this matter, by which their lying and fabrication are known? Suppose they argued about what they have knowledge of; how, then, do they argue in this state? Thus, before one even examines what their statement contains of falsehood, the corruption of their claim is known. In this verse there is evidence that it is not permissible for a person to say or to dispute about what he has no knowledge of. And His saying: {And Allah is the Protector of the believers}; so whenever the faith of the servant grows strong, Allah takes him under His kindness, makes easy for him the ease, and keeps him away from the hardship.

This is a blessing from God upon this community, in that He informed them of the scheming of their enemies from among the People of the Book, and that, out of their eagerness to lead the believers astray, they devise various wicked schemes. A group of them said: {Believe in what has been revealed to those who believe at the beginning of the day}; that is, at its first part, "and disbelieve at its end, so that perhaps they may turn back from their religion." For when they see you turning back while they believe you to have knowledge, they will become doubtful about their religion and say: "Had they not seen in it something that displeases them, and that does not agree with the earlier Books, they would not have turned back." This is their scheme. But God is the One who guides whom He wills, and He is the One in whose hand is bounty, which He bestows upon whom He wills. So He has singled you out, O this community, with what He did not single out for others. Those scheming ones did not realize that the religion of God is the truth; when its reality reaches the hearts, its adherent, over the course of time, increases only in faith and certainty, and doubts do not increase him except in adherence to his religion, and in praise of God and thanks to Him for having bestowed it upon him. As for their saying: {Or that anyone should be given the like of what you were given, or that they should argue with you before your Lord}; it means that what moved them to these reprehensible acts was envy, transgression, and fear of being argued against, as God the Exalted said: {Many of the People of the Book wish they could turn you back into disbelievers after your belief, out of envy from themselves, after the truth has become clear to them}; the verse.

{75} He, exalted is He, informs us that among the People of the Book there is a group of trustworthy people: if you entrusted them with a qintar (a large sum of money, meaning a great quantity of wealth), they would return it to you. And among them there is a group of treacherous people who would betray you in the smallest matter. Despite this shameful treachery, they make excuses with false justifications, saying: {There is no blame upon us concerning the unlettered} (al-ummiyyin); that is, there is no sin upon us if we betray them and deem their wealth lawful for us, because they have no sanctity. He, exalted is He, said: {And they speak falsely against Allah while they know it}; that is, the greatest distress is upon them. They combined betrayal, contempt for the Arabs, and lying against Allah, while knowing that. They are not like one who does this out of ignorance and misguidance.

{76} Then He, exalted is He, said: {Yes}; that is, the matter is not as they claimed. {Whoever fulfills his covenant and fears Allah}; that is, whoever upholds the rights of Allah and the rights of His creation, for this is the one who is righteous (al-muttaqi), and Allah loves him. Conversely, whoever is otherwise, who does not fulfill his covenant and contracts that are between him and the creation, nor observes the fear of Allah, then Allah abhors him, and He will requite him with the greatest punishment.

{77} That is: those who sell their religion for the goods of this world, choosing the meagre trifles of worldly life and seeking them through false oaths and broken covenants, these are they of whom ﴿Allah will not speak to them, nor look at them on the Day of Resurrection, nor purify them, and theirs will be a painful punishment﴾. That is: the wrath of Allah has become due upon them and His punishment has become binding upon them; they are deprived of His reward and prevented from being purified (tazkiyah), which means cleansing. Rather, they will come to the Resurrection defiled by crimes and soiled by grave sins.

{78} That is: among the People of the Book there is indeed a group who distort the Book of God. ﴿They twist their tongues with the Book so that you may think it is from the Book﴾. This includes both distortion of wording (al-tahrif al-lafzi) and distortion of meaning (al-tahrif al-ma'nawi). Then, along with this grievous distortion, they give the impression that it is from the Book, while they are liars in this, and they openly speak falsehood against God, and they know their own state and the evil of their final end.

{79-80} That is: it is impossible and utterly inconceivable for a human being whom God has favored with revelation, the Book and prophethood, and to whom He has given legal authority, that he should command people to worship him, or to worship the prophets and the angels and take them as lords. For this is disbelief (kufr). How much more so, when he was sent with Islam, which is opposed to disbelief in every respect; how could he then command its opposite? This is among the impossible things, because his condition, what he is upon, and the virtues and distinctions with which God has favored him require complete servitude and perfect submission to God, the One, the Subduer. This is a reply to the delegation of Najran, when their arrogance went to extremes, their state and pride reached the point that they said: "Do you command us, O Muhammad, to worship you?" when he had commanded them to worship God and obey Him. So the Creator (al-Bari') made clear the negation of what they said, and that their words and the words of those like them on this matter are evidently false.

{81–82} This is an announcement from Him, exalted is He, that He took the covenant and pledge of all the prophets, because of what He had given them and bestowed upon them of the Book and wisdom, which necessitates their complete fulfilment of the right of Allah and their perfect carrying out of it: that if there came to them a messenger confirming what was with them, sent with what they were sent with of tawhid (monotheism), truth, justice, and the foundational principles upon which the sacred laws (shara'i') agree, they would believe in him and support him. So they acknowledged this, confessed it, and bound themselves to it. He made them witness it, He bore witness against them, and He threatened whoever opposed this covenant.

This is a general matter among the prophets: that their path is one, and that the call of each of them is one upon which they all agreed and entered into a pact. The comprehensive meaning of this is that the covenant of belief in and support for Muhammad (ﷺ) was taken from all of them. Whoever claims to be among their followers, this is their religion which Allah took from them, which they acknowledged and confessed. So whoever turns away from following Muhammad (ﷺ), while claiming to be among their followers, is a wrongdoer (fasiq), outside the obedience of Allah, a denier of the Messenger whom he claims to follow, and opposed to his path. In this is the establishment of proof and evidence against everyone among the People of the Scriptures and the religions who does not believe in Muhammad (ﷺ), and that they cannot believe in their messengers whom they claim to follow until they believe in their leader and their seal (ﷺ).

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 3, verses 83–85:

{83–85} It has already been mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah that these foundations, which are the foundations of faith (iman) that Allah has commanded this Ummah to hold, are agreed upon by the Books and the Messengers, that they are the true objective directed at every person, and that they are the true religion and Islam; and that whoever seeks other than them, his deeds are rejected and he has no religion on which he can rely. So whoever turns away from them and renounces them, where will he go? To the worship of trees, stones and fires, or to taking rabbis (ahbar) and monks (ruhban) and crosses as lords, or to denying the Lord of the worlds (ta'til), or to the false religions that are inspired by the devils? All of these, in the Hereafter, are among the losers.

{86–88} This means that it is utterly far-fetched that Allah would guide a people who had recognized faith, entered into it, and testified that the Messenger is true, and then turned back upon their heels, retreating and breaking their covenant. For they recognized the truth and rejected it. And whoever is characterized by this state, Allah punishes him with an inversion (intikas) and a turning of the heart, as a recompense for him, since he recognized the truth and abandoned it, and preferred falsehood; so Allah leaves him to what he has chosen for himself. These are they upon whom is ﴿the curse of Allah, and of the angels, and of mankind, all together﴾; abiding in the curse and the punishment, ﴿their punishment will not be lightened, nor will they be reprieved﴾, when the command of Allah comes, because Allah gave them a lifespan in which one who would remember could remember, and the warner came to them.

{89–91} Then, Exalted is He, excepted from this threat those who repent from their disbelief and sins and reform their faults, for Allah forgives them what they have done before and pardons what they have committed in the past. But whoever disbelieves and persists in his disbelief, increasing in nothing but disbelief until he dies upon it, these are the ones who have strayed from the path of guidance and who travel the path of wretchedness, and they have deserved by this the painful punishment. ﴿So there will not be for them any helper from the punishment of Allah﴾, and even if they were to offer the earth filled with gold in order to ransom themselves with it, it would not benefit them in the least. So we seek refuge in Allah from disbelief and its branches.

{92} That is, "You will not attain" and reach "righteousness" (al-birr), which is a comprehensive term for all good, and it is the path that leads to Paradise, "until you spend from what you love" of your best and purest wealth. Spending from what is good and beloved to the souls is among the greatest proofs of the generosity of the soul and its being characterized by noble character, its mercy and its tenderness. It is also among the most indicative proofs of love for Allah and of preferring His love over love of wealth, to which souls have been created with a strong attachment. Whoever prefers the love of Allah over the love of his own self has reached the highest summit of perfection. Likewise, whoever spends good things and does good to the servants of Allah, Allah will do good to him and will enable him to perform deeds and possess character traits that cannot be attained without this state. Moreover, whoever performs this spending in this manner, his performance of the remaining righteous deeds and virtuous characteristics is all the more fitting and deserving. Although spending from good things is the most complete state, whatever the servant spends, whether little or much, of good or otherwise, "indeed Allah is Knowing of it," and He will reward every spender according to his deed: He will reward him in this world with a swift replacement, and in the Hereafter with a delayed bounty.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 3, verses 93–94:

{93–94} Among the matters with which the Jews cast doubt on the prophethood of Jesus and Muhammad (ﷺ) is that they claimed abrogation (naskh) is invalid, and that it is impossible for a prophet to come who contradicts the prophet before him. God refuted them with a matter they themselves know. They acknowledge that all food was permitted to the Children of Israel before the revelation of the Torah, except for a few things which Israel, that is Jacob (peace be upon him), prohibited for himself, and which he abstained from because of an illness that afflicted him. Then the Torah contains many prohibitions that abrogated what had been lawful before. Say to them, if they deny this: ﴿Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful﴾, according to your claim that there is no abrogation, no making lawful, and no making unlawful. This is one of the most eloquent arguments: to argue against a person with a matter that he himself says and acknowledges and does not deny. If he submits to the truth, that is what is obligatory; and if he refuses and does not submit after this clarification, his lying, fabrication, wrongdoing, and the invalidity of what he adheres to become evident. This is what has actually happened with the Jews.

Ibn Sa'di's commentary on Surah 3, verses 96–97:

{96–97} Allah, exalted is He, informs us of the greatness of His Sacred House, and that it is the first house which Allah established on earth for His worship and the remembrance of His name. In it are blessings, various kinds of guidance, and a great abundance of benefits and interests for all the worlds. In it are clear signs that remind of the standing-places of Ibrahim the Friend (Khalil) and his movements during the Hajj, and after him they remind of the standing-places of the Master of the Messengers and their Imam. In it is security, so that whoever enters it is secure, by decree (qadar) and by legal ruling (shar') and religion.

When it contained these matters, whose summaries are these and whose details are many, Allah made its Hajj obligatory upon the accountable people who are able to find a way to it. The one who is able to reach it, by whatever suitable mount and provision he can take for himself, is included. For this reason He used this wording, which can be applied to all existing and future means of transport. This is one of the signs of the Qur'an, in that its rulings are suitable for every time and every circumstance, and complete well-being cannot be achieved without them. Whoever submits to this and performs it is among the guided believers, and whoever disbelieves and does not commit to performing the Hajj of His House has left the religion, {And whoever disbelieves, then indeed Allah is Free of need from the worlds}.

{102–105} In these verses, God urges His believing servants to give thanks for His great blessings: to be mindful of Him with the mindfulness that is due to Him (taqwa), to perform His obedience and abandon His disobedience, doing so sincerely for Him alone; to establish their religion and hold fast to His rope (habl), which He sent down to them and made the means of connection between them and Him, namely His religion (din) and His Book; to unite upon that and not to be divided; and to persist in this until death.

He reminds them of their state before this blessing: they were enemies, scattered, and He united them through this religion, joined their hearts, and made them brothers. They were on the brink of a pit of Fire, and He rescued them from wretchedness and set them on the path of happiness. Therefore He said: ﴿Thus Allah makes clear to you His signs, that you may be guided﴾, pointing to the thanks due to Allah and to holding fast to His rope.

He commanded them to complete this condition, and the strongest means by which they could establish their religion is that a group among them should take on the task, so that sufficiency is achieved: ﴿calling to good﴾, which is the religion in its foundations, its branches, and its laws; ﴿enjoining what is right﴾, which is what is known to be good by the Law and by reason; and ﴿forbidding what is wrong﴾, which is what is known to be ugly by the Law and by reason. ﴿And those are the successful﴾, those who attain every sought goal and are saved from every feared thing.

This group includes people of knowledge and teaching, those who take up preaching and admonishing people in general and in particular, and the muhtasibun (those who enjoin good and forbid evil in public matters), who compel people to establish the prayers, give zakat, and observe the laws of the religion, and forbid them from evil deeds.

Thus, whoever calls people to good, whether in general or in particular, or gives public or private counsel, is included in this noble verse.

Then He forbade them from following the path of those who were divided, to whom the religion and the clear proofs came, which obligated them to uphold it and to be united, yet they became divided, disagreed, and became sects (shiya'). This did not arise from ignorance and misguidance, but from knowledge combined with evil intent and the transgression of some against others. For this reason He said: ﴿And those will have a great punishment﴾. Then He explained when this great punishment will occur and when this painful torment will befall them, saying:

{106–107} He, may He be exalted, informs of the difference among creation on the Day of Resurrection in happiness and wretchedness. God, may He be exalted, will admit them into the Gardens and pour upon them all kinds of honors, and they will abide therein forever. The faces of the people of wretchedness, who denied His messengers, disobeyed His command, and divided their religion into sects, will be blackened. He praises Himself also for what He has prepared for those people of reward and for the others of punishment, and that this is the requirement of His bounty, His justice, and His wisdom. He does not wrong His servants, nor diminish their deeds, nor punish anyone without his sin, nor lay upon him the burden of another. When He mentioned that to Him belongs the command and the law (al-shar'), He mentioned that to Him belongs the complete dominion, the disposal of affairs, and the authority, and so He said:

{109} ﴿And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and to God all matters are returned﴾; so He recompenses the doers of good for their goodness and the doers of evil for their disobedience. He is the Judge among His servants in this world and the Hereafter, and whatever else among the created beings is subject to judgment, having no share in the affair at all.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 3, verses 110–111:

{110–111} This is a declaration by God of the superiority of this Ummah (community) for these qualities, by which they were distinguished and surpassed all other nations: that they are the best of people for mankind, in sincere counsel, in love of goodness, in calling (to the faith), in teaching and guidance, in enjoining what is good and forbidding what is evil, and in combining the perfecting of others and the striving for their benefit as far as is possible, with the perfecting of the self through faith in God and the fulfilment of the rights of faith. And [He declares] that if the People of the Book had believed in the like of what you have believed in, they would have been guided and it would have been better for them; but only a few of them believe, while most of them are defiant transgressors, going out of obedience to God and obedience to His Messenger, waging war against the believers and striving with all their power to harm them. Yet, despite that, they will not harm the believers except with a little hurt by the tongue; and if they fight you, they will turn their backs, then they will not be helped. This has come to pass as God foretold: when they fought the Muslims, they turned their backs, and God gave the Muslims victory over them.

**Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 3, verse 112:**

{112} This is an information from Allah, exalted is He, that the Jews have been struck with humiliation; they are fearful wherever they are found, and nothing secures them except a covenant (mu'ahadah) and a cause through which they are safe, by submitting to the rulings of Islam and acknowledging the jizyah (poll tax), or by a rope {from the people}; that is, when they are under the authority and guardianship of others, as their condition has been witnessed previously and subsequently. For indeed, in the latest period they did not manage to establish their temporary kingdom in Palestine except through the support of the major powers and their paving the way for them with every means {and they incurred wrath from Allah}; that is, Allah has become angry with them and punished them with humiliation and destitution. The cause of that is their disbelief in the signs of Allah and their killing of the prophets {without right}, that is, not out of ignorance, but out of transgression and obstinacy. These varied punishments upon them are {because they disobeyed and used to transgress}. So Allah, exalted is He, has not wronged them, nor punished them without sin; rather, what He has brought upon them is due to their transgression, their aggression, their disbelief, their denial of the messengers, and their monstrous crimes.

{113–114} When Allah mentioned the deviators among the People of the Book, He made clear the condition of the upright among them, and that among them is a community (ummah) who uphold the foundations of the religion and its branches: ﴿They believe in Allah and the Last Day, and enjoin what is good﴾; and that is all goodness, ﴿and forbid what is wrong﴾; and that is all evil, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And among the people of Musa is a community who guide by the truth and by it act justly﴾; and ﴿they hasten in good works﴾. Hastening to good works is an added degree beyond merely doing them. It is a description of them as doing good, being quick to undertake it, and perfecting it with everything that completes it of obligatory and recommended acts.

{115} Then Allah, the Exalted, explained that whatever good they did, whether little or much, Allah will surely accept it, since it proceeded from faith and sincerity. ﴿So it will not be denied them﴾; that is, it will not be disregarded regarding what they did, nor will it be wasted. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of the God-fearing﴾; and they are those who stood up to good deeds and abandoned what is forbidden, seeking the pleasure of Allah and desiring His reward.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 3, verses 116–117:

{116–117} Allah, exalted is He, explains that the disbelievers who disbelieved in the signs of Allah and denied His messengers, no one will rescue them from the punishment of Allah, no helper will benefit them, and no intercessor will intercede for them with Allah. Their wealth and their children, which they used to prepare for hardships and calamities, will not avail them anything. And their expenditures, which they spent in this world to support their falsehood, will come to nothing. Their likeness is {like}: a field whose crop was struck by {a wind} that is {severe, in which is a frost}; that is, an intense cold or a scorching fire, which destroyed that field. That happened because of their wrongdoing. Allah did not wrong them, nor does He punish them without a sin; rather, they wronged themselves. This is like His saying, exalted is He: {Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to avert [people] from the way of Allah. They will spend it; then it will be a regret for them; then they will be overcome.}

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 3, verses 116–117:

{116–117} Allah, exalted is He, explains that the disbelievers who disbelieved in the signs of Allah and denied His messengers, no one will rescue them from the punishment of Allah, no helper will benefit them, and no intercessor will intercede for them with Allah. Their wealth and their children, which they used to prepare for hardships and calamities, will not avail them anything. And their expenditures, which they spent in this world to support their falsehood, will come to nothing. Their likeness is {like}: a field whose crop was struck by {a wind} that is {severe, in which is a frost}; that is, an intense cold or a scorching fire, which destroyed that field. That happened because of their wrongdoing. Allah did not wrong them, nor does He punish them without a sin; rather, they wronged themselves. This is like His saying, exalted is He: {Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to avert [people] from the way of Allah. They will spend it; then it will be a regret for them; then they will be overcome.}

{118–119} This is a warning from God to His servants against taking disbelievers as allies, intimate confidants (bitanah) or close friends, to whom they confide and reveal the secrets of the believers. He made clear to His believing servants the matters that necessitate disassociation from taking them as confidants: that they {do not spare you corruption} (la yalunakum khabalan), meaning they are eager and do not fall short in bringing harm upon you. Hatred has already appeared in their speech and in the slips of their tongues, and what their breasts conceal of hatred and enmity {is greater} than what has appeared to you of their words and deeds. If you have understanding and intellect, then God has made their matter clear to you. Moreover, what is the reason for loving them and taking them as allies and confidants, when you know from them the great deviation in religion and their repayment of your kindness? You adhere to the religions of the messengers, believing in every messenger God sent and every book God revealed, while they disbelieve in the most noble books and the most exalted messengers. You extend to them compassion and love of a kind they do not repay even in the smallest measure. So how can you love them when they do not love you, and when they flatter and feign friendship toward you? When they meet you, {they say, "We believe"}, but when they are alone {with their own kind}, {they bite their fingertips at you} out of intense rage and hatred toward you and your religion. God, the Exalted, said: {Say, "Die in your rage"}; that is, you will see the honor of Islam and the humiliation of disbelief, which will grieve you, and you will die in your rage, never attaining the healing of that by what you intend. {Indeed, God is Knower of what is in the breasts} (inna Allaha 'alimun bidhat al-sudur); therefore He made clear to His believing servants what the breasts of the enemies of the religion, from among the disbelievers and hypocrites, conceal.

{120} {If good touches you} ('izz, victory, well-being and goodness) {it distresses them, and if an evil befalls you} (by the enemy gaining the upper hand or the occurrence of some worldly calamity) {they rejoice at it}. This is the description of the enemy whose enmity is severe. Having made clear the intensity of their enmity and explained the wicked qualities they possess, God commanded His believing servants to be patient and to hold fast to taqwa (God-consciousness), and [He told them] that if they do so, the plots of their enemies will not harm them in the least, for God encompasses them and their deeds and the schemes with which they plot against you. He promised you that, when you uphold taqwa, they will not harm you at all, so do not doubt that this will come to pass.

{121} This was the day of Uhud, when the Prophet (ﷺ) went out with the Muslims, after the polytheists had brought their army close to Uhud. The Prophet (ﷺ) stationed them in their positions, set them in their places, and arranged them in a remarkable order, which shows the perfection of his judgment and his complete skill in the sciences of strategy (siyasah), just as he was perfect in every situation. {And Allah is Hearing, Knowing} — nothing of your affairs is hidden from Him.

{122} {When two groups among you were about to lose heart} — they were the clans of Banu Salamah and Banu Harithah — but the Creator took care of them with His kindness, His protection, and His guidance. {And upon Allah let the believers rely} — for when they rely upon Him, He suffices them, helps them, and protects them from what would harm them in their religion and their worldly life.

In this verse and similar ones is the obligation of tawakkul (trust in Allah), and that a servant's reliance is in proportion to his faith. Tawakkul is the servant's dependence upon his Lord for the attainment of his benefits and the repelling of his harms.

When He mentioned their condition at Uhud and the calamity that befell them, He included in it a reminder of His victory and favor upon them at Badr, so that they would be thankful to their Lord, and so that this would ease that. He said:

{123} {And Allah had already given you victory at Badr when you were weak} — in your number and your equipment. They were three hundred and some odd men, with few mounts and poor weapons, while their enemies were nearly a thousand, in full readiness and weaponry. {So fear Allah that you may be grateful} — to the One who blessed you with His victory.

{124} {When you said to the believers, as a means of giving good tidings and strengthening their hearts}: {Is it not sufficient for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?}

{125} {Yes. If you are patient and fear Allah, and they come upon you immediately} — that is, from their present assault, {your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels marked} — that is, marked with the sign of the brave. People have differed as to whether this reinforcement involved the angels directly fighting, as some have said, or whether it was a strengthening from Allah for His believing servants and the casting of terror into the hearts of the polytheists, as many of the commentators have said, and this is indicated by His saying:

{126} {And Allah did not make it except as good tidings for you and to reassure your hearts thereby. And victory is not except from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise}. In this is the point that a servant should not rely upon means, but rely upon Allah; means and their abundance serve only to bring tranquility to hearts and steadfastness in goodness.

{127} {That He may cut off a portion of those who disbelieved or repel them so they return frustrated} — that is, the victory of Allah for His believing servants amounts only to cutting off a part of the disbelievers, or turning them back in their rage, having gained no good, just as He turned them back on the day of the Trench after they had come against the believers in full force. Allah turned them back in their rage, frustrated.

{128} When the Prophet ﷺ was struck at the Battle of Uhud, his lower front tooth (ruba'iyyah) was broken and his head was wounded, he began to say: "How can a people prosper who have wounded the face of their Prophet and broken his tooth?" So Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse, and made clear that the whole matter belongs to Allah, and that the Messenger ﷺ has no share in the matter at all, for he is a servant among the servants of Allah, and all of them are under the servitude of their Lord, managed and not managers. As for those against whom you invoked curses, O Messenger, or whose success and guidance seemed remote, Allah, if He wills, will turn to them in forgiveness and enable them to enter Islam, and He did so, for most of those people were guided by Allah and embraced Islam. And if He wills, He will punish them, for they are wrongdoers who deserve the punishments and torment of Allah.

{129} He, exalted is He, informs that He is the Disposer of the upper and lower worlds, and that He turns in forgiveness to whomever He wills, forgiving him, and abandons whomever He wills, punishing him. ﴿And Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful﴾. Of His necessary attributes is perfect forgiveness and mercy, and the existence of their requirements in creation and in command: He forgives those who repent and shows mercy to those who take up the causes that necessitate mercy. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And obey Allah and the Messenger that you may receive mercy﴾.

The second volume of Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman fi Tafsir Kalam al-Rahman (Tafsir al-Karim al-Rahman, "The Easy Exposition of the Generous, the Merciful, in the Exegesis of the Speech of the All-Merciful"), by its compiler, the poor one in need of God, Abd al-Rahman ibn Nasir ibn Abd Allah ibn Sa'di, may God forgive him, his parents, and all Muslim men and women, the living among them and the dead, by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful. Amen.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, and in Him we seek help, and upon Him we rely. Lord, make it easy and help, O Generous.

All praise is due to Allah. We praise Him, seek His help, and ask His forgiveness, and we seek refuge in Allah from the evils of our souls and the bad consequences of our deeds. Whomever Allah guides, none can misguide; and whomever He leaves astray, none can guide. I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah, alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger (ﷺ), and He sent abundant peace upon him. He, exalted is He, says:

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 3, verse 130–136:

{130} It was mentioned in the introduction to this tafsir that the servant should observe the commands and prohibitions both in himself and in others. When God Most High commands him with something, he must first know its limit (hadd) and what he is commanded to do, so that he can carry it out. Once he knows this, he should strive and seek God's help in fulfilling it in himself and in others, according to his ability and capacity. Likewise, when he is forbidden from something, he should know its limit, what enters into it and what does not, and then strive and seek his Lord's help in abandoning it. This must be observed in all the divine commands and prohibitions. These noble verses include commands and qualities of goodness, which God ordered and urged the performance of, and He informed of the reward of their people, and prohibitions which He urged be abandoned.
Perhaps the wisdom (hikmah) behind placing these verses in the middle of the story of Uhud, God knows best, is that it has previously been mentioned that God promised His believing servants that if they are patient and fear God, He would grant them victory over their enemies and cause the enemies to be humbled before them, as in His saying: ﴿But if you are patient and fear God, their scheming will not harm you at all﴾. Then He said: ﴿But if you are patient and fear God, and they come upon you suddenly, your Lord will reinforce you...﴾ and the verses that follow. So it is as if souls longed to know the qualities of God-consciousness (taqwa) through which victory, success and happiness are attained. God therefore mentioned in these verses the most important qualities of taqwa, which if the servant performs them, then performing anything else is all the more fitting and befitting.
What indicates what we have said is that God mentioned the word taqwa in these verses three times: once unrestricted, which is His saying: ﴿prepared for the God-conscious (muttaqin)﴾, and twice restricted, so He said: ﴿fear God (ittaqu Allah)﴾ and ﴿fear the Fire (ittaqu al-nar)﴾.
As for His saying: ﴿O you who believe﴾: every instance in the Qur'an of His saying "O you who believe, do such-and-such, or abandon such-and-such" indicates that faith is the motivating and obligating cause for complying with that command and avoiding that prohibition, because faith is the complete affirmation of what must be affirmed, which necessitates the actions of the limbs. He forbade them from consuming riba (usury) multiplied manifold, and this was what the people of jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic ignorance) and those who do not care about the legal commands were accustomed to: when a debt fell due upon a debtor who was unable to pay and had nothing, they would say to him, "Either you pay what you owe, or we will extend the term and increase what is upon you." The poor man, pressed and wishing to relieve his creditor and accept this for the sake of immediate ease, would thereby see his obligation multiplied manifold, without any benefit or gain. In His saying ﴿multiplied manifold﴾ there is an indication of the severity of its abomination through its quantity, and an indication of the wisdom behind its prohibition, that God forbade it because of the injustice it contains. God obligated granting respite to the insolvent debtor and leaving what he owes without increase, so compelling him to pay more than that is multiplied injustice. It is therefore incumbent upon the believing, God-fearing person to abandon it and not approach it, because abandoning it is one of the requirements of taqwa, and success depends upon taqwa. For this reason He said: ﴿And fear God, that you may prosper﴾.

{131} ﴿And fear the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers﴾, by abandoning what necessitates entering it, namely disbelief and sins, according to their varying degrees. All sins, and especially major sins, lead to disbelief; indeed they are among the qualities of disbelief for whose people God prepared the Fire. Abandoning sins saves one from the Fire and protects one from the wrath of the Almighty, while acts of goodness and obedience bring about the pleasure of the Merciful, entry into the Gardens, and attainment of mercy. For this reason He said:

{132} ﴿And obey God and the Messenger﴾, by performing the commands in compliance and avoiding the prohibitions, ﴿that you may receive mercy﴾. Obedience to God and obedience to His Messenger are among the causes of obtaining mercy, as He Most High said: ﴿My mercy encompasses all things, so I will decree it for those who fear God and give zakat...﴾ and the verses that follow.

{133} Then God Most High commanded them to hasten toward His forgiveness and to attain His Garden, whose breadth is the heavens and the earth. How then about its length, which He prepared for the God-conscious? They are its people, and the deeds of taqwa are what lead to it.

{134} Then He described the God-conscious and their deeds, saying: ﴿those who spend in ease and in hardship﴾; that is, in their state of difficulty and ease: if they are well-off, they spend abundantly, and if they are in straitened circumstances, they do not belittle any act of kindness, even if it is little. ﴿And those who restrain anger﴾: that is, when they receive harm from others that would cause them anger, namely their hearts being filled with rage which would necessitate retaliation by word or deed. These do not act according to the dictates of human nature; rather they suppress the anger in their hearts and patiently refrain from responding to the one who wronged them. ﴿And who pardon people﴾: pardoning people includes pardoning everyone who wrongs you by word or deed. Pardon is more complete than restraint, because pardon is leaving off punishment together with forgiveness toward the offender. This only comes from one who has adorned himself with beautiful character and purified himself of vile character, and who trades with God and pardons God's servants out of mercy toward them, kindness to them, and dislike of evil befalling them, and so that God may pardon him, and his reward is with his generous Lord, not with the poor servant, as He said: ﴿So whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is upon God﴾.
Then He mentioned a state more general than others, better, higher and more exalted, which is ihsan (excellence), so He said: ﴿And God loves the doers of good (muhsinin)﴾. Ihsan is of two types: ihsan in the worship of the Creator, and ihsan to the created.
As for ihsan in the worship of the Creator, the Prophet ﷺ explained it with his saying: "That you worship God as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, indeed He sees you."
As for ihsan to the created, it is conveying religious and worldly benefit to them and repelling religious and worldly harm from them. This includes commanding them to do good, forbidding them from evil, teaching their ignorant, admonishing their heedless, giving sincere counsel to both common and elite, striving to unite their word, and delivering charity and obligatory and recommended expenditures to them according to their varying conditions and differing attributes. It includes giving generously, withholding harm, and bearing harm patiently, as God described the God-conscious in these verses. Whoever performs these matters has fulfilled the right of God and the right of His servants.

Then He mentioned their seeking pardon from their Lord for their offenses and sins, saying:

{135} ﴿And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves﴾; that is, if there proceeds from them a great sinful act or something less than that, they hasten to repentance and seeking forgiveness, and remember their Lord and what He threatened for the disobedient and promised for the God-conscious, so they ask Him for forgiveness of their sins and concealment of their faults, along with ceasing from them and regretting them. For this reason He said: ﴿and do not persist in what they have done while they know﴾.

{136} ﴿Those﴾; those described by these qualities, ﴿their reward is forgiveness from their Lord﴾ which removes from them every harm, ﴿and gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾, containing everlasting bliss, joy, happiness, radiance, goodness, delight, palaces, elegant lofty dwellings, fruitful beautiful trees and flowing rivers in those good dwellings, ﴿wherein they abide forever﴾, not turning away from them, not seeking any substitute for them, and the bliss they are in not changing; ﴿and excellent is the reward of the workers﴾, who worked for God a little and were given much in return. At morning the people praise the night journey, and at the time of reward the worker finds his wage complete and abundant.
These noble verses are among the proofs of Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah that deeds enter into faith, contrary to the Murji'ah. The point of the proof is completed only by mentioning the verse in Surah al-Hadid parallel to these verses, which is His saying: ﴿Race toward forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whose width is like the width of the heaven and the earth, prepared for those who believe in God and His messengers﴾. In that verse, only the word of faith in Him and His messengers is mentioned, whereas here He said: ﴿prepared for the God-conscious﴾, then described the God-conscious by these financial and physical deeds, which indicates that these God-conscious people are those believers described by these qualities. Then He Most High said:

These noble verses are among the proofs of Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah that deeds enter into faith, contrary to the Murji'ah. The point of the proof is completed only by mentioning the verse in Surah al-Hadid parallel to these verses, which is His saying: ﴿Race toward forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whose width is like the width of the heaven and the earth, prepared for those who believe in God and His messengers﴾. In that verse, only the word of faith in Him and His messengers is mentioned, whereas here He said: ﴿prepared for the God-conscious﴾, then described the God-conscious by these financial and physical deeds, which indicates that these God-conscious people are those believers described by these qualities. Then He Most High said:

{137} These noble verses, and what follows them concerning the story of Uhud, are a consolation from Allah, may He be exalted, to His believing servants. He comforts and reassures them, and informs them that generations and many nations passed before them who were tested, and the believers among them were afflicted with fighting the disbelievers. They continued in alternating fortunes and struggle until Allah made the final outcome belong to the God-fearing (muttaqun) and victory belong to His believing servants. In the end, dominion was secured over the deniers, and Allah humbled them through the victory of His messengers and their followers. ﴿So travel through the earth﴾ with your bodies and your hearts, ﴿and see how was the end of the deniers﴾. For you will find them none but punished with various kinds of worldly chastisement; their dwellings have been laid waste, their loss has become clear to everyone, their might, their kingdom, their arrogance and their pride have departed and vanished. Is there not in this the greatest proof and the clearest witness to the truth of what the messengers brought, and to the wisdom of Allah by which He tests His servants, so that He may try them and distinguish the truthful from the liars? For this reason, He, may He be exalted, said:

{138} ﴿This is a clarification for mankind﴾; that is, a manifest indication that clarifies for mankind the truth from falsehood, and the people of happiness from the people of wretchedness. It refers to what Allah inflicted upon the deniers. ﴿And a guidance and an admonition for the God-fearing﴾, because they are the ones who benefit from the signs; it guides them to the path of rectitude and admonishes them and restrains them from the way of error. As for the rest of mankind, it is a clarification for them, by which the proof of Allah is established against them, so that whoever perishes perishes after clear evidence. It is also possible that the reference in His saying ﴿This is a clarification for mankind﴾ is to the Great Qur'an and the Wise Reminder, and that it is a clarification for mankind in general, and a guidance and admonition for the God-fearing in particular. Both meanings are true.

{139} Allah, the Exalted, says, encouraging His believing servants, strengthening their resolve, and spurring up their determination: ﴿And do not weaken nor grieve﴾; that is: do not weaken and be feeble in your bodies, and do not grieve in your hearts when calamity befalls you and you are tried with this affliction. For grief in the hearts and weakness in the bodies add a calamity upon you and serve as a help to your enemy against you. Rather, encourage your hearts, make them patient, drive grief away from them, and stand firm in fighting your enemy. Allah mentioned that weakness and grief are not fitting nor proper for them, since they are the superior ones in faith and in hope for the victory and reward of Allah. The believer who seeks what Allah has promised of worldly and otherworldly reward should not have such traits. Therefore He said: ﴿And you will be superior if you are [true] believers.﴾

Then He consoled them for what had befallen them of defeat, and explained the great wisdoms that follow from it, saying:

{140} ﴿If a wound has touched you, [know that] a wound has touched the people likewise.﴾ You and they are equal in the wound, but you hope from Allah for what they do not hope for, as He said: ﴿If you are suffering, then indeed they suffer as you suffer, but you hope from Allah that for which they do not hope.﴾
Among the wisdoms in this is that Allah grants from this abode to the believer and the disbeliever, the righteous and the wicked alike, and He alternates the days among people: a day for this group and a day for the other group, because this worldly abode is transient and perishing. This is unlike the Hereafter, which is exclusively for those who believe. ﴿And that Allah may make evident those who believe﴾: this is also among the wisdoms, that Allah tests His servants with defeat and affliction so that the believer may be distinguished from the hypocrite. For if victory continued for the believers in all encounters, whoever did not truly desire Islam would enter it. So when some kinds of affliction occur in some encounters, the one who truly believes, who desires Islam in adversity and ease, in hardship and facility, is distinguished from one who is not like that. ﴿And [that] He may take from among you martyrs.﴾
This is also among some of the wisdoms, for martyrdom is among the highest stations with Allah, and there is no way to attain it except through the occurrence of its causes. This is from His mercy toward His believing servants: that He has ordained for them causes that souls dislike, so that He may grant them the lofty stations and everlasting bliss that they love. ﴿And Allah does not love the wrongdoers﴾: those who wronged themselves and held back from fighting in His cause. It seems that in this there is an allusion to blaming the hypocrites and that they are hated by Allah; for this reason He discouraged them from fighting in His cause. Had they wished to go out, they would have prepared equipment for it, but Allah disliked their setting out, so He held them back, and it was said: ﴿Sit with those who sit.﴾

{141} ﴿And that Allah may purify those who believe﴾: this is also among the wisdoms, that Allah purifies the believers by this from their sins and faults. This indicates that martyrdom and fighting in the cause of Allah expiate sins and remove faults. And that Allah may also purify the believers from others, namely the hypocrites, so that they become free of them and recognize the believer from the hypocrite.
Also among the wisdoms is that He decrees this in order to destroy the disbelievers, that is, to be a cause of their destruction and eradication through punishment. For when they are victorious they transgress and increase in their rebellion upon their rebellion, deserving thereby to be hastened into punishment, as a mercy to His believing servants. Then Allah, the Exalted, says:

{142} ﴿Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while Allah has not yet made evident those of you who fought [in His cause] and made evident the steadfast?﴾ This is a rhetorical question of denial: that is, do not suppose, nor let it occur to your minds, that you will enter Paradise without hardship and enduring hardships in the cause of Allah and seeking His pleasure. For Paradise is the highest of aims and the best thing for which competitors compete, and the greater the goal, the greater its means and the deed that leads to it. Rest is not reached except by abandoning rest, and bliss is not attained except by abandoning comfort. But the hardships of this world that afflict the servant in the cause of Allah, when the soul is accustomed to them, trained in them, and aware of their outcome, turn, for people of insight, into gifts in which they rejoice and which they do not mind. That is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills. Then Allah, the Exalted, rebuked them for their lack of patience regarding a matter they used to wish for and desire to happen, saying:

{143} ﴿And you had certainly wished for death before you encountered it﴾: this is because many of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, who had missed Badr, wished that Allah would bring them to an occasion in which they could exert their utmost effort. Allah said to them: ﴿Then you have seen it﴾; [that is, you have seen] what you wished for with your own eyes, ﴿while you were looking on.﴾ What, then, is the matter with you and abandoning patience? This is a state that is neither fitting nor proper, especially for one who wished for that and had what he wished for. For it is obligatory upon him to exert effort and spend his utmost capacity in that. In this verse there is evidence that wishing for martyrdom is not disliked. The indication is that Allah confirmed them in their wish and did not denounce them for it; He denounced them only for not acting in accordance with its requirement. And Allah knows best. Then Allah, the Exalted, says:

{142} ﴿Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while Allah has not yet made evident those of you who fought [in His cause] and made evident the steadfast?﴾ This is a rhetorical question of denial: that is, do not suppose, nor let it occur to your minds, that you will enter Paradise without hardship and enduring hardships in the cause of Allah and seeking His pleasure. For Paradise is the highest of aims and the best thing for which competitors compete, and the greater the goal, the greater its means and the deed that leads to it. Rest is not reached except by abandoning rest, and bliss is not attained except by abandoning comfort. But the hardships of this world that afflict the servant in the cause of Allah, when the soul is accustomed to them, trained in them, and aware of their outcome, turn, for people of insight, into gifts in which they rejoice and which they do not mind. That is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills. Then Allah, the Exalted, rebuked them for their lack of patience regarding a matter they used to wish for and desire to happen, saying:

{143} ﴿And you had certainly wished for death before you encountered it﴾: this is because many of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, who had missed Badr, wished that Allah would bring them to an occasion in which they could exert their utmost effort. Allah said to them: ﴿Then you have seen it﴾; [that is, you have seen] what you wished for with your own eyes, ﴿while you were looking on.﴾ What, then, is the matter with you and abandoning patience? This is a state that is neither fitting nor proper, especially for one who wished for that and had what he wished for. For it is obligatory upon him to exert effort and spend his utmost capacity in that. In this verse there is evidence that wishing for martyrdom is not disliked. The indication is that Allah confirmed them in their wish and did not denounce them for it; He denounced them only for not acting in accordance with its requirement. And Allah knows best. Then Allah, the Exalted, says:

{144} God, exalted is He, says: {Muhammad is but a messenger; [other] messengers have passed away before him}. That is, he is not an innovation among the messengers; rather, he is of the same kind as the messengers before him. Their duty was to convey the message of their Lord and carry out His commands. They were not immortal, and their remaining alive was not a condition for obeying God's commands. Rather, it is obligatory upon the nations to worship their Lord at all times and in every state. For this reason He said: {So if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels?}, that is, by abandoning what he brought you of faith, or jihad, or other things. God, exalted is He, said: {And whoever turns back on his heels will not harm God at all}; he only harms himself. God is free of need of him, will establish His religion, and will honor His believing servants.

When God, exalted is He, reproached those who turned back on their heels, He praised those who remained steadfast with His Messenger and complied with the command of their Lord, saying: {And God will reward the grateful}. Gratitude is not realized except by performing servitude to God, exalted is He, in every state. This noble verse contains guidance from God, exalted is He, to His servants that they should be in a state in which the loss of a leader, however great he may be, does not shake them from their faith or from some of its requirements. This is achieved only by preparing, in every matter of religion, a number of people of competence in it, so that when one of them is lost another can take up his task. It also requires that the general body of believers intend to establish the religion of God and to strive in its defense to the extent of their ability, and that they have no particular attachment to one leader over another. In this state their affairs will be firmly settled and their matters will be set right.

Also in this verse is the greatest evidence for the virtue of the Foremost of the Truthful, Abu Bakr, and of his companions who fought the apostates after the Messenger of God (ﷺ), for they are the masters of the grateful.

{145} Then God, exalted is He, informed that all souls are bound to their appointed terms by the permission, decree, and judgment of God. Whoever is decreed by destiny to die, dies, even without a cause; and whoever He wills to remain alive, even if every cause befalls him, it will not harm him before his term arrives. This is because God has decreed, ordained, and recorded it until a specified term: {When their term comes, they cannot delay it an hour, nor can they advance it}. Then God, exalted is He, informed that He gives people of the reward of this world and the Hereafter what their wills are attached to, saying: {Whoever desires the reward of this world, We will give him of it; and whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter, We will give him of it}. God, exalted is He, said: {To each We extend, both these and those, from the bounty of your Lord; and the bounty of your Lord is not restricted. Look how We have favored some of them over others; and the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in favor} {And We will reward the grateful}. He did not mention their reward so that this would indicate its abundance and greatness, and so that it would be known that the reward is according to the degree of gratitude, in its little and its much, and its goodness.

{146} This is a consolation for the believers, an exhortation to follow them and to act as they acted, and that this is a matter that has occurred before, the way of Allah having continued to operate in this manner. So He said: ﴿And how many a prophet fought, and with him were many devoted followers﴾; that is, how many prophets fought, and with them were many groups of their followers whom the prophets had nurtured with faith and righteous deeds, so that they suffered killing, wounds and other things. ﴿Yet they did not weaken for what befell them in the way of Allah, nor did they weaken, nor did they submit﴾; that is, their hearts did not weaken, their bodies did not falter, and they did not submit, meaning they did not humble themselves before their enemy. Rather, they endured, held firm and encouraged themselves. For this reason He said: ﴿And Allah loves the steadfast﴾.

{147} Then He mentioned their words and their appeal to their Lord, saying: ﴿And their only words were: "Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excesses in our affairs"﴾. Excess (al-israf) is: exceeding the limit into what is forbidden. They knew that sins and excess are among the greatest causes of abandonment, and that freeing oneself from them is among the causes of victory, so they asked their Lord for their forgiveness. Furthermore, they did not rely on the patience they had exerted their utmost effort in, but depended upon Allah and asked Him to make their feet firm when meeting the disbelieving enemies and to grant them victory over them. Thus they combined patience with avoidance of its opposite, repentance, seeking forgiveness, and seeking victory from their Lord. Without doubt, Allah gave them victory and granted them the outcome in this world and the Hereafter. For this reason He said:

{148} ﴿So Allah gave them the reward of this world﴾, namely victory, triumph and spoils, ﴿and the good reward of the Hereafter﴾, which is attaining the pleasure of their Lord and everlasting bliss free from all distress. This was only because they performed good deeds for Him, so He repaid them with the best recompense. For this reason He said: ﴿And Allah loves the doers of good﴾ in worshipping the Creator and dealing with creation. Among excellence (ihsan) is to act in fighting the enemies as these believers acted. Then the Exalted said:

{149} This is a prohibition from Allah to the believers against obeying the disbelievers among the hypocrites (munafiqun) and the polytheists (mushrikun), for if they obey them, they will want for them nothing but evil, and their aim is to return them to disbelief, whose end is loss and ruin.

{150} Then He informed them that He is their Protector (mawla) and their Helper (nasir). In this there is information to them of that and good tidings, that He takes charge of their affairs with His kindness and protects them from all kinds of evil. Implicit in this is an exhortation for them to take Him alone as their Protector and Helper, above everyone else.

{151} Among His protection and help for them is that He promised them that He would cast terror (ru'b) into the hearts of their enemies among the disbelievers, that is, the great fear that prevents them from many of their aims. And Allah, exalted is He, has done so. This occurred because the polytheists, after they had withdrawn from the Battle of Uhud, consulted among themselves and said: "How can we withdraw after we have killed those of them whom we killed and defeated them, while we have not yet uprooted them?" So they resolved upon that, but Allah cast terror into their hearts, and they withdrew defeated.

There is no doubt that this is among the greatest of victories, because it has already been established that the victory of Allah for His believing servants does not go beyond one of two matters: either He cuts off a portion of those who disbelieve, or He humiliates them so that they turn back defeated. This is of the second kind. Then he mentioned the cause that necessitates the casting of terror into the hearts of the disbelievers, saying: {Because they associated with Allah that for which He had sent down no authority}; i.e., that is because of what they took besides Him of rivals and idols, which they took according to their whims and corrupt desires, without any proof or evidence, and they severed themselves from the guardianship of the One, the Most Merciful. Therefore the polytheist is terrified before the believers, not relying on a firm support, and having no refuge in every difficulty and hardship. This is his state in this world, but in the Hereafter it is worse and greater. For this reason He said: {And their abode is the Fire}; i.e., their place of settlement to which they return, and from which they have no exit, {and wretched is the abode of the wrongdoers}, because of their wrongdoing and transgression, the Fire has become their abode.
