{152} That is: {And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you} of victory, so He granted you victory over them until you routed them, by His permission, and you were killing them, until you became, through your own act, a cause of your own harm and a helper to your enemies against you. Then weakness (al-fashl), which is feebleness and faintheartedness, appeared among you, {and you disputed about the matter}, which involved abandoning Allah's command to be united and not to be divided. So you differed: some said, "We shall remain at our position where the Prophet ﷺ placed us," and others said, "What is our staying here, when the enemy has been defeated and there is no longer any danger?" Thus you disobeyed the Messenger and abandoned his command, {after He had shown you what you love}, namely the rout of your enemies. This is because the obligation upon one whom Allah has favored with what He loves is greater than upon others. Therefore the obligation in this situation in particular, and in other situations in general, is to comply with the command of Allah and His Messenger. {Among you are those who desire this world}; they are those for whom that which was decreed for them was decreed, {and among you are those who desire the Hereafter}; they are those who adhered to the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and held firm where they were ordered to stand.

{Then He turned you away from them}; that is, after these matters had occurred among you, Allah turned your faces away from them, so the facing of your enemy became a trial and a test from Allah for you, so that the believer may be distinguished from the disbeliever, and the obedient from the disobedient, and so that Allah might expiate from you, through this calamity, what had proceeded from you. Hence He said: {And certainly He has pardoned you. And Allah is full of bounty toward the believers}; that is, possessed of great bounty toward them, in that He bestowed upon them Islam, guided them to its laws, pardoned their misdeeds, and rewarded them for their afflictions. Among His bounty toward the believers is that He does not decree for them any good or any calamity except that it is good for them: if prosperity reaches them and they give thanks, He recompenses them with the reward of the grateful; and if adversity reaches them and they are patient, He recompenses them with the reward of the patient.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 3, verse 153–154:

{153} Allah, exalted is He, reminds them of their state at the time of their flight from the battle, and rebukes them for it, saying: {When you were going up [the slopes] and not turning aside for anyone}; i.e., you were hastening in flight. {And not turning aside for anyone}; i.e., none of you was turning to look at another, but rather your only concern was to flee and escape from the battle, while in fact there was no great danger upon you, since you were not the last of the people facing the enemy and engaging in the fight. Rather, {the Messenger was calling you from your rear}; i.e., from the side of the people, saying: "To me, O servants of Allah!" But you did not turn to him, nor did you incline toward him. Fleeing in itself warrants blame, and the Messenger's call, which required that you prefer him over yourselves, makes your failure to respond even more blameworthy. {So He rewarded you}; i.e., He requited you for your deed {with grief upon grief}; i.e., grief followed by grief: grief over the loss of victory and of the spoils, grief over your defeat, and grief that overshadowed all other griefs, which was your hearing that Muhammad (ﷺ) had been killed.
However, Allah, in His kindness and good regard for His servants, made the combination of these matters good for the believing servants, so He said: {So that you would not grieve over what escaped you}; of victory and triumph, {nor over what befell you}; of defeat, killing and wounds, once you were assured that the Messenger (ﷺ) had not been killed. Those calamities became light for you, and you rejoiced in his being alive, which consoles every affliction and trial. How rich are the secrets and wisdoms contained within afflictions and trials, and all of this proceeds from His knowledge and perfect awareness of your deeds, your outward and inward states. Hence He said: {And Allah is Acquainted with what you do}. It is also possible that the meaning of His words {so that you would not grieve over what escaped you nor over what befell you} is: He decreed that grief and calamity upon you so that your souls would become accustomed and trained to patience in the face of calamities, and so that bearing hardships would become easy for you.

{154} {Then He sent down upon you, after the grief}, which had befallen you, {security, drowsiness overtaking a faction of you}. There is no doubt that this was a mercy to them, a kindness, a strengthening of their hearts and an increase in tranquility, for the fearful person is not overtaken by sleep because of the fear in his heart; when fear departs from the heart, sleep may come upon him. This faction upon whom Allah bestowed drowsiness were the believers, who had no concern except the establishment of Allah's religion, the pleasure of Allah and His Messenger, and the welfare of their Muslim brothers. As for the other faction, {whom their own selves had made anxious}, they had no concern other than themselves, because of their hypocrisy or weakness of faith; therefore the sleep that overtook others did not overtake them. {They say: "Do we have any say in the matter?"}; this is an interrogative of denial, meaning: we have no part in the matter, i.e., victory and dominance. They thus harbored evil thoughts about their Lord, about His religion, and about His Prophet, and thought that Allah would not complete the affair of His Messenger, and that this defeat was decisive and final against the religion of Allah.
Allah answered them, saying: {Say: "Indeed, the matter entirely belongs to Allah"}. The "matter" encompasses both the decreed command and the legislated command; all things are by Allah's decree and destiny, and their final outcome is victory and triumph for His friends and the people of His obedience, even if what happened to them befell them. {They conceal within themselves what they do not reveal to you}; meaning the hypocrites. Then He clarified the matter they were concealing, saying: {They say: "If we had any say in the matter"}; i.e., if we had an opinion and counsel in this event, {we would not have been killed here}. This is a denial on their part, a rejection of Allah's decree, a belittling of the opinion of the Messenger of Allah and of his companions, and a self-praise on their part. So Allah answered them by saying: {Say: "Even if you had been in your houses"}, which are the furthest thing from places of expected killing, {those for whom killing had been decreed would have come out to their places of death}. Causes, however great, benefit only when they are not opposed by destiny and decree; when destiny opposes them, they benefit nothing, and it is inevitable that Allah carry out what He has written in the Preserved Tablet concerning death and life. {And that Allah may test what is in your breasts}; i.e., He may examine what is within them of hypocrisy, faith and weakness of faith, {and purify what is in your hearts}, of the whisperings of Satan and the blameworthy qualities that result from them. {And Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts}; i.e., of what they contain and what they conceal. Thus His knowledge and wisdom required that He decree such causes by which the hidden contents of the breasts and the secret matters would become manifest. Then Allah, exalted is He, said:

There is no doubt that this was a mercy to them, a kindness, a strengthening of their hearts and an increase in tranquility, for the fearful person is not overtaken by sleep because of the fear in his heart; when fear departs from the heart, sleep may come upon him. This faction upon whom Allah bestowed drowsiness were the believers, who had no concern except the establishment of Allah's religion, the pleasure of Allah and His Messenger, and the welfare of their Muslim brothers. As for the other faction, {whom their own selves had made anxious}, they had no concern other than themselves, because of their hypocrisy or weakness of faith; therefore the sleep that overtook others did not overtake them. {They say: "Do we have any say in the matter?"}; this is an interrogative of denial, meaning: we have no part in the matter, i.e., victory and dominance. They thus harbored evil thoughts about their Lord, about His religion, and about His Prophet, and thought that Allah would not complete the affair of His Messenger, and that this defeat was decisive and final against the religion of Allah.
Allah answered them, saying: {Say: "Indeed, the matter entirely belongs to Allah"}. The "matter" encompasses both the decreed command and the legislated command; all things are by Allah's decree and destiny, and their final outcome is victory and triumph for His friends and the people of His obedience, even if what happened to them befell them. {They conceal within themselves what they do not reveal to you}; meaning the hypocrites. Then He clarified the matter they were concealing, saying: {They say: "If we had any say in the matter"}; i.e., if we had an opinion and counsel in this event, {we would not have been killed here}. This is a denial on their part, a rejection of Allah's decree, a belittling of the opinion of the Messenger of Allah and of his companions, and a self-praise on their part. So Allah answered them by saying: {Say: "Even if you had been in your houses"}, which are the furthest thing from places of expected killing, {those for whom killing had been decreed would have come out to their places of death}. Causes, however great, benefit only when they are not opposed by destiny and decree; when destiny opposes them, they benefit nothing, and it is inevitable that Allah carry out what He has written in the Preserved Tablet concerning death and life. {And that Allah may test what is in your breasts}; i.e., He may examine what is within them of hypocrisy, faith and weakness of faith, {and purify what is in your hearts}, of the whisperings of Satan and the blameworthy qualities that result from them. {And Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts}; i.e., of what they contain and what they conceal. Thus His knowledge and wisdom required that He decree such causes by which the hidden contents of the breasts and the secret matters would become manifest. Then Allah, exalted is He, said:

{155} He, exalted is He, informs about the state of those who fled on the day of Uhud, what caused them to flee, and that it was from the whispering (taswil) of Satan. He gained power over them because of some of their sins: they were the ones who gave him access to themselves and empowered him through the acts of disobedience they committed, since these are a vehicle and an entry point for him. Had they held fast to the obedience of their Lord, he would have had no authority over them. Allah, the Most High, said: ﴿Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them﴾. Then He informed that He pardoned them after they had done what requires accountability; otherwise, had He taken them to account, He would have uprooted them completely. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving﴾ toward the sinners and those who err, through what He enables them to do of repentance, seeking forgiveness, and the expiating afflictions; ﴿Forbearing﴾, who does not hasten to punish those who disobey Him but gives them time, and calls them to turn back in repentance to Him and to turn toward Him. Then, if they repent and turn back, He accepts it from them and makes it as though no sin had proceeded from them and no fault had come from them. So all praise is due to Allah for His kindness.

{156} Almighty Allah forbids His believing servants from imitating the disbelievers, who do not believe in their Lord nor in His decree and destiny, such as the hypocrites and others. He forbids them from imitating them in everything, and in this particular matter, namely that they say to their brethren in religion or in lineage, {when they travel in the land}; that is, they travel for trade, {or were raiders}; that is, they are warriors, and then killing or death befalls them. They dispute the decree and say: {If they had stayed with us, they would not have died or been killed}. This is a lie on their part, for Allah the Exalted has said: {Say: "Even if you had been in your houses, those decreed to be slain would have come out to their place of death."} However, this denial did not benefit them; rather, Allah makes this saying and this belief a source of regret in their hearts, so their calamity increases. As for the believers, they know that this occurs by the decree of Allah, so they believe and submit, and Allah guides their hearts and makes them firm, and thereby lightens the calamity upon them. Allah responds to them, saying: {And Allah gives life and causes death}; that is, He alone does this, so no caution avails against decree. {And Allah is Seeing of what you do}; so He will recompense you for your deeds and your denial.

{157} Then Allah informs that being killed in His cause, or dying in it, contains no deficiency or harm; rather, it is something that competitors should vie for, because it is a means leading to and attaining the forgiveness of Allah and His mercy, and that is better than what the people of this world amass of their worldly wealth.

{158} And that creatures, when they die or are killed in whatever state, their return is to Allah and their final destination is to Him, and He will recompense each one according to his deeds. So where is escape except to Allah, and there is no protector for creatures except holding fast to the rope of Allah.

{159} That is: by the mercy of Allah toward you and your companions. Allah bestowed upon you that you were gentle toward them, lowered your wing to them, showed them tenderness, and made your character good toward them, so they gathered around you, loved you, and carried out your command. {And had you been harsh}; that is, bad-tempered {hard-hearted}; that is, severe, {they would have dispersed from around you}, because this would repel them and make them hate the one who displays this bad character. Good character from the leader in religion draws people to the religion of Allah and makes them desire it, along with the praise and special reward for its possessor; and bad character from the leader in religion repels people from the religion and makes them hate it, along with the blame and special punishment for its possessor. So if this infallible Messenger is told by Allah what He tells him, then what about others? Is it not among the most obligatory of obligations and the most important of important matters to follow his noble character and to deal with people in the manner in which he (ﷺ) dealt with them, with gentleness, good character, and winning hearts, in compliance with the command of Allah and to attract the servants of Allah to the religion of Allah?

Then Allah the Exalted commanded him to pardon them for what they had done of shortcoming in his right (ﷺ), and to ask forgiveness for them for shortcoming in the right of Allah, thus combining pardon with kindness. {And consult them in the matter}; that is, in the affairs that require consultation, reflection, and deliberation, for in consultation there are benefits and interests, religious and worldly, that cannot be enumerated:

Among them: consultation is an act of worship through which one draws near to Allah.

Among them: it soothes their hearts and removes what arises in hearts at events. Whoever holds authority over people, when he gathers the people of opinion and virtue and consults them on an incident, their souls are reassured, they love him, and they know that he does not act arbitrarily against them, but looks to the general and overall interest of all. So they exert their utmost effort and ability in obeying him, knowing his striving for the interests of the public. By contrast, one who is not like this, they hardly love him with sincere love nor obey him, and if they obey him, it is not complete obedience.

Among them: consultation refines thoughts through exercising them in what they were made for, so it increases the intellects.

Among them: what consultation produces of correct opinion, for the one who consults hardly errs in his action, and if he errs or his goal is not achieved, he is not blameworthy.

If Allah says this to His Messenger (ﷺ), who is the most complete of people in intellect, the most abundant in knowledge, and the most excellent in judgment: {And consult them in the matter}, then what about others? Then He the Exalted said: {And when you have decided}; that is, upon a matter after consulting about it, if it requires consultation, {then rely upon Allah}; that is, depend upon the power and strength of Allah, disavowing your own power and strength. {Indeed, Allah loves those who rely upon Him}, who take refuge in Him.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 3, verse 160:

{160} That is: if Allah aids you with His help and support, ﴿then none can overcome you﴾. Even if all who are in its regions gathered against you, along with whatever number and equipment they have, (none could overcome you), because Allah cannot be overpowered. He has subdued His servants and holds their forelocks, so no creature moves except by His permission, and none is still except by His permission. ﴿But if He forsakes you﴾ and leaves you to yourselves, ﴿then who is there that can help you after Him?﴾ Then you will surely be forsaken, even if all of creation were to help you. Included within this is the command to seek help from Allah, to rely upon Him, and to disavow any power or strength of one's own. For this reason He said: ﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely.﴾ The placing of the object before the verb indicates restriction, meaning: rely upon Allah and not upon other than Him, because it is known that He alone is the Helper. Reliance upon Him is monotheism that attains the desired goal, while reliance upon other than Him is shirk, which does not benefit its doer but rather harms him. In this verse there is the command to rely upon Allah alone, and that a servant's reliance is in proportion to his faith.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 3, verse 161:

{161} Ghulul (embezzlement): it is concealing something from the spoils of war and betraying in any property a person is entrusted with. It is forbidden by consensus (ijma'), and indeed it is among the major sins (kaba'ir), as this noble verse and other texts indicate. God, exalted is He, informed that it is not fitting or proper for a Prophet to commit embezzlement, because embezzlement, as you know, is among the greatest of sins and the worst of defects.

God, exalted is He, has protected His prophets from everything that would defile them or discredit them. He made them the best of mankind in character, the purest of souls, the most pure, the most virtuous, and free from every defect. He made them the bearers of His message and the source of His wisdom: {God knows best where to place His message}. Thus, by the mere knowledge of the servant of any one of them, he is certain of their freedom from every matter that would discredit them, and he needs no proof for what their enemies have said about them, because knowing their prophethood necessarily entails the rejection of such charges. For this reason, God used a form of expression that precludes the occurrence of the act from them, saying: {And it is not for a Prophet to embezzle}; that is, such a thing is impossible and inconceivable for those whom God has chosen for prophethood. Then He mentioned the threat against whoever embezzles, saying: {And whoever embezzles will bring what he embezzled on the Day of Resurrection}; that is, he will bring it carried on his back, whether it be an animal, goods, or something else, and he will be punished with it on the Day of Resurrection. {Then every soul will be paid in full what it has earned}; the embezzler and others alike will each be repaid their reward and their burden according to the measure of their earning. {And they will not be wronged}; that is, nothing will be added to their evil deeds, and nothing of their good deeds will be diminished.

Reflect on the excellence of this qualification in this noble verse: when it mentioned the punishment of the embezzler, that he will come on the Day of Resurrection with what he embezzled, and when it wished to mention the full payment and recompense, and since restricting the statement to the embezzler could lead one to infer that other kinds of workers might not be paid in full, it used a general expression that encompasses him and others.

{162–163} He, exalted is He, informs that one whose aim is the pleasure of his Lord and acting in what pleases Him is not equal to one who is not like that, one who is absorbed in sins and displeasing to his Lord. These two are not equal in the judgment of Allah, in the wisdom of Allah, or in the natural disposition of the servants of Allah. ﴿Is one who is a believer like one who is defiantly disobedient? They are not equal.﴾ For this reason He said here: ﴿They are of varying degrees with Allah.﴾ That is, all of these differ in their degrees and ranks according to the differences in their deeds.

Those who follow the pleasure of Allah strive to attain the high degrees, the lofty ranks and the elevated chambers, and Allah gives them of His bounty and generosity according to the measure of their deeds. Those who follow the displeasure of Allah strive to descend into the depths of the Fire, down to the lowest of the low, each according to his deeds. Allah is All-Seeing of their deeds; nothing of them is hidden from Him. Rather, He has known them and recorded them in the Preserved Tablet, and He has entrusted His noble, trustworthy angels to write them down, preserve them and keep account of them.

This is the favour which God bestowed upon His servants, the greatest of blessings, indeed its very root: the favour of this noble Messenger, through whom God rescued them from misguidance and preserved them from ruin. He said: ﴿Certainly did Allah confer [His] favor upon the believers when He sent among them a messenger from themselves﴾; they knew his lineage, his condition, and his tongue, being of their own people and tribe, a counselor to them and compassionate toward them, ﴿reciting to them His verses﴾, teaching them their words and their meanings, ﴿and purifying them﴾ from polytheism, sins, vices, and all the blameworthy qualities of character, ﴿and teaching them the Book﴾; this may refer to the genus of the Book, which is the Qur'an, so that His saying ﴿reciting to them His verses﴾ means the cosmic signs; or the meaning of "the Book" here is writing, so that He favoured them by teaching them writing and the script through which knowledge is acquired and preserved. ﴿And wisdom﴾; this is the Sunnah, which is the twin of the Qur'an; or it means placing things in their proper places and knowing the secrets of the Shari'ah. Thus he combined for them the teaching of the rulings, that by which the rulings are implemented, and that by which their benefits and fruits are perceived. By these great matters they surpassed all created beings and became among the rabbinic scholars. ﴿And indeed, they had been before in clear error﴾; before the sending of this Messenger, they did not know the path that leads to their Lord, nor what purifies and cleanses souls, but rather they did whatever their ignorance made appealing to them, even if that contradicted the intellects of all beings!

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 3, verses 165–168:

{165} This is a consolation from Allah Most High to His believing servants when what befell them at the Battle of Uhud happened to them, and about seventy of them were killed. Allah said: You have {inflicted twice as much} [on the polytheists at the Battle of Badr], for you killed seventy of their leaders and took seventy captive. So let the matter be easy for you and let the calamity be light upon you, especially since you and they are not equal: your slain are in Paradise and their slain are in the Fire. {You say: "How is this?"}, meaning: from where has this affliction and defeat come upon us? {Say: "It is from yourselves."} When you disputed and disobeyed after He had shown you what you love. So turn your blame upon yourselves and beware of the causes that lead to ruin. {Indeed, Allah is over all things competent}; so beware of having an evil opinion of Allah, for He is capable of granting you victory, but He has perfect wisdom in testing you and in this affliction of yours. Had Allah willed, He would have taken vengeance upon them, but [He willed it so] that He might test some of you by means of others.

{166–167} Then He informed that what befell them on the day the two hosts met, the host of the Muslims and the host of the polytheists at Uhud, of killing and defeat, was by His leave, His decree and His divine destiny; it cannot be averted and it must occur. When the decree of destiny is carried out, nothing remains but submission to it, and that He ordained it for great wisdoms and abundant benefits, and that by it the believer is distinguished from the hypocrite. Those who, when they were commanded to fight, {and it was said to them: "Come, fight in the way of Allah"}, meaning: in defence of the religion of Allah, protecting it and seeking the pleasure of Allah, {or repel [the enemy]}, from your sacred things and your land, if you had no sound intention. But they refused that and made excuses, saying: {"Had we known there would be fighting, we would have followed you."} That is: had we known that fighting would take place between you and them, we would have followed you. They were lying in this, for they knew and were certain, and everyone knew, that these polytheists were filled with rage and fury against the believers for what they had suffered at their hands, that they had spent their wealth and gathered whatever men and numbers they could, and had come with a great army, intending the believers in their own city, burning with eagerness to fight them. For one in such a state, how could it be imagined that no fighting would take place between them and the believers? Especially since the Muslims had left Medina and gone out to face them. This is impossible; but the hypocrites thought this excuse would deceive the believers. Allah said: {They were nearer to disbelief that day than to faith; they say with their mouths what is not in their hearts}. This is a particular trait of the hypocrites: they show by their words and deeds the opposite of what they conceal within their hearts and inner selves. Among this is their saying: {"Had we known there would be fighting, we would have followed you"}, for they had known that fighting would occur. From this verse is derived the principle of undertaking the lesser of two harms to avert the greater of them, and of performing the lesser of two benefits when unable to attain the greater, for the hypocrites were commanded to fight for the religion, and if they did not do so, then to defend their families and homelands. {And Allah knows best what they conceal}, so He will manifest it to His believing servants and will punish them for it.

{168} Then Allah Most High said: {Those who said of their brothers, while they sat at home: "If they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed."}, meaning: they combined staying behind from jihad with objecting to and denying the decree and destiny of Allah. Allah replied to them: {Say: "Then avert death from yourselves, if you are truthful"}, meaning: repel death from yourselves, [and show] that had they obeyed you they would not have been killed, which you are not able to do and do not have the power to do. These verses show that a servant may have in him a trait of disbelief and a trait of faith, and he may be closer to one of them than to the other.

Allah replied to them: {Say: "Then avert death from yourselves, if you are truthful"}, meaning: repel death from yourselves, [and show] that had they obeyed you they would not have been killed, which you are not able to do and do not have the power to do. These verses show that a servant may have in him a trait of disbelief and a trait of faith, and he may be closer to one of them than to the other.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 3, verses 165–168:

{165} This is a consolation from Allah Most High to His believing servants when what befell them at the Battle of Uhud happened to them, and about seventy of them were killed. Allah said: You have {inflicted twice as much} [on the polytheists at the Battle of Badr], for you killed seventy of their leaders and took seventy captive. So let the matter be easy for you and let the calamity be light upon you, especially since you and they are not equal: your slain are in Paradise and their slain are in the Fire. {You say: "How is this?"}, meaning: from where has this affliction and defeat come upon us? {Say: "It is from yourselves."} When you disputed and disobeyed after He had shown you what you love. So turn your blame upon yourselves and beware of the causes that lead to ruin. {Indeed, Allah is over all things competent}; so beware of having an evil opinion of Allah, for He is capable of granting you victory, but He has perfect wisdom in testing you and in this affliction of yours. Had Allah willed, He would have taken vengeance upon them, but [He willed it so] that He might test some of you by means of others.

{166–167} Then He informed that what befell them on the day the two hosts met, the host of the Muslims and the host of the polytheists at Uhud, of killing and defeat, was by His leave, His decree and His divine destiny; it cannot be averted and it must occur. When the decree of destiny is carried out, nothing remains but submission to it, and that He ordained it for great wisdoms and abundant benefits, and that by it the believer is distinguished from the hypocrite. Those who, when they were commanded to fight, {and it was said to them: "Come, fight in the way of Allah"}, meaning: in defence of the religion of Allah, protecting it and seeking the pleasure of Allah, {or repel [the enemy]}, from your sacred things and your land, if you had no sound intention. But they refused that and made excuses, saying: {"Had we known there would be fighting, we would have followed you."} That is: had we known that fighting would take place between you and them, we would have followed you. They were lying in this, for they knew and were certain, and everyone knew, that these polytheists were filled with rage and fury against the believers for what they had suffered at their hands, that they had spent their wealth and gathered whatever men and numbers they could, and had come with a great army, intending the believers in their own city, burning with eagerness to fight them. For one in such a state, how could it be imagined that no fighting would take place between them and the believers? Especially since the Muslims had left Medina and gone out to face them. This is impossible; but the hypocrites thought this excuse would deceive the believers. Allah said: {They were nearer to disbelief that day than to faith; they say with their mouths what is not in their hearts}. This is a particular trait of the hypocrites: they show by their words and deeds the opposite of what they conceal within their hearts and inner selves. Among this is their saying: {"Had we known there would be fighting, we would have followed you"}, for they had known that fighting would occur. From this verse is derived the principle of undertaking the lesser of two harms to avert the greater of them, and of performing the lesser of two benefits when unable to attain the greater, for the hypocrites were commanded to fight for the religion, and if they did not do so, then to defend their families and homelands. {And Allah knows best what they conceal}, so He will manifest it to His believing servants and will punish them for it.

{168} Then Allah Most High said: {Those who said of their brothers, while they sat at home: "If they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed."}, meaning: they combined staying behind from jihad with objecting to and denying the decree and destiny of Allah. Allah replied to them: {Say: "Then avert death from yourselves, if you are truthful"}, meaning: repel death from yourselves, [and show] that had they obeyed you they would not have been killed, which you are not able to do and do not have the power to do. These verses show that a servant may have in him a trait of disbelief and a trait of faith, and he may be closer to one of them than to the other.

**{169}** These noble verses contain the virtue and honour of the martyrs and what Allah has bestowed upon them of His grace and kindness. Within them is also consolation for the living concerning their slain, comfort for them, and encouragement to fight in the cause of Allah and to seek martyrdom. So He said: ﴿And do not think of those who have been killed in the cause of Allah as dead.﴾ That is, in fighting the enemies of the religion, intending thereby to make the word of Allah supreme. ﴿Dead﴾ means: let it not occur to your mind or assumption that they have died, been lost, and departed from the pleasure of this worldly life and its enjoyment of its splendour, the loss of which one fears might make a person cowardly in fighting and indifferent to martyrdom. ﴿Rather,﴾ they have obtained what is greater than anything that competitors compete for. They are ﴿alive with their Lord﴾ in the abode of His honour. The phrase "with their Lord" indicates the elevation of their rank and their nearness to their Lord. ﴿They are provided for﴾ with kinds of bliss whose description none knows except the one who bestowed it upon them.

**{170}** And along with this, ﴿rejoicing in what Allah has given them of His bounty﴾; that is, they are delighted with that, their eyes are cooled by it and their souls rejoice in it, because of its goodness, abundance, and greatness, the complete pleasure in attaining it, and the absence of anything that spoils it. Thus Allah combined for them the bliss of the body through provision and the bliss of the heart and spirit through rejoicing in what He has given them of His bounty. Their bliss and joy were thereby completed, and they began ﴿rejoicing in those who have not yet joined them from behind them﴾; that is, some of them give glad tidings to others of the arrival of their brothers who have not yet joined them, and that they will attain what they attained. ﴿No fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾; that is, they rejoice at the removal of what is feared for them and for their brothers, which entails complete joy.

**{171}** ﴿They rejoice in favour from Allah and bounty﴾; that is, some of them congratulate others with the greatest thing one can be congratulated upon, which is the favour of their Lord, His bounty and His kindness. ﴿And that Allah does not waste the reward of the believers﴾; rather He multiplies it, gives thanks for it, and increases for them from His bounty what their striving does not reach.

In these verses is an affirmation of the bliss of the barzakh (intermediate realm), that the martyrs are in the highest station with their Lord, and in them is the meeting of the souls of the righteous, their visiting one another, and their giving glad tidings to one another.

{172–173} When the Prophet (ﷺ) returned from Uhud to Madinah and heard that Abu Sufyan and those with him among the polytheists had resolved to return to Madinah, he called his Companions to go out. So they went out despite their wounds, responding to Allah and His Messenger and obeying Allah and His Messenger. They reached Hamra' al-Asad, and someone came to them and said: {Indeed, the people have gathered against you}; and they intended to annihilate you, to frighten and terrify them. But this only increased them in faith in Allah and in reliance upon Him, {and they said: "Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs"}; that is, sufficient for us in everything that concerns us, {and the best Disposer of affairs}; the one to whom the management of His servants is entrusted and who looks after their interests.

{174} {So they returned}; that is, they went back {with favor from Allah and bounty, and no harm touched them}. The news reached the polytheists that the Messenger and his Companions had come out against them, and those among them who had stayed behind regretted it. Allah cast terror into the hearts of the polytheists, and they continued returning to Makkah. The believers returned with favor from Allah and bounty, since He bestowed upon them the success of going out in this state and of relying upon their Lord. Furthermore, a complete reward for a full military expedition was recorded for them. Because of their good conduct in obeying their Lord and their piety in abstaining from His disobedience, there is a great reward for them, and this is Allah's bounty upon them.

{175} Then He, exalted is He, said: {It is only the Shaytan who frightens his allies}; that is, the terrorizing of those who were frightened by the polytheists, and His saying that they {have gathered against you...}, is a call from the callers of Shaytan, by which he frightens his allies whose faith has been lost or weakened. {So do not fear them, but fear Me, if you are believers}; that is, do not fear the polytheists, the allies of Shaytan, for their forelocks are in the hand of Allah and they act only by His decree. Rather, fear Allah, who supports His allies who fear Him and respond to His call.

In this verse is the obligation to fear Allah alone, and that it is a requirement of faith. The servant's fear of Allah is in proportion to the strength of his faith. Praiseworthy fear is that which restrains the servant from what Allah has forbidden.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 3, verses 176–177:

{176} The Prophet (ﷺ) was eager for the creation and strove hard for their guidance, and he would grieve when they did not accept guidance. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And do not let those who hasten into disbelief grieve you﴾, due to their intense desire for it and their eagerness for it, ﴿Indeed, they will never harm Allah at all.﴾ Allah is the Supporter of His religion, the Strengthener of His Messenger, and the Executor of His command without them. So do not concern yourself with them or pay them any heed. They only harm, and strive toward harming, themselves, by losing faith in this world and by incurring a painful punishment in the Hereafter. This is due to their lowliness before Allah and their fall from His sight and His will, that He not grant them any share of His reward in the Hereafter. He forsook them and did not grant them success in what He granted to His allies. And whoever He wills good for, He does so out of justice and wisdom, knowing that they are not purified toward guidance and are not receptive to right guidance, because of the corruption of their character and the badness of their intention.

{177} Then He informed that those who chose disbelief over faith and desired it, with the desire of one who spends what he loves of wealth to buy what he loves of goods, ﴿will never harm Allah at all﴾. Rather, the harm of their deeds returns upon themselves. For this reason He said: ﴿And for them is a painful punishment.﴾ And how could they harm Allah at all?! They have renounced faith in the utmost renunciation and have desired disbelief in the Most Merciful with complete desire. So Allah is Free of need of them. He has appointed for His religion, from among His righteous and pure servants other than them, and has prepared for it, from among those whom He has approved for His support, people of insight and intellect, and men of sound judgment and mature minds. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say, "Believe in it or do not believe. Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall down on their faces in prostration..."﴾ [the verses].

He has appointed for His religion, from among His righteous and pure servants other than them, and has prepared for it, from among those whom He has approved for His support, people of insight and intellect, and men of sound judgment and mature minds. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say, "Believe in it or do not believe. Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall down on their faces in prostration..."﴾ [the verses].

{178} That is: Let not those who disbelieve in their Lord, who reject His religion and wage war against His Messenger, suppose that Our leaving them in this worldly life, Our not uprooting them, and Our granting them respite is good for them or an expression of Our love for them. No, the matter is not as they claim. Rather, that is for an evil that Allah intends for them, and an increase in punishment and retribution added to their torment. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, We grant them respite only that they may increase in sin; and for them is a humiliating punishment.﴾ Thus Allah, exalted is He, gives the wrongdoer respite until his transgression increases and his disbelief accumulates; then when He seizes him, He seizes him as the Mighty, the Omnipotent. So let the wrongdoers beware of being given respite, and let them not suppose that they can escape the Great, the Most High.

{179} That is: it was not within the wisdom of God to leave the believers in the state of mixture and non-differentiation that you are in, until He distinguishes the wicked from the good, the believer from the hypocrite, and the truthful from the liar. Nor was it within His wisdom to make His servants aware of the unseen that He knows about them. Therefore His overwhelming wisdom required that He test His servants and try them, by means of which the wicked is distinguished from the good, through various kinds of trial and examination. So God sent His messengers, commanded obedience to them, submission to them, and belief in them, and promised those who believe and are mindful of Him a great reward. Thus people were divided, according to their following of the messengers, into two groups: obedient and disobedient, believers and hypocrites, Muslims and disbelievers, so that reward and punishment would be consequent upon that, and so that His justice, His grace, and His wisdom would be manifest to His creation.

{180} That is: those who are stingy, i.e., who withhold what they have of the bounty Allah has given them, whether wealth, standing, knowledge, or other things that Allah has bestowed upon them and favoured them with, and whom He commanded to spend of that which does not harm them upon His servants. They were stingy with that, held it back, and grudged it to the servants of Allah, and they thought it was good for them, when in fact it is evil for them in their religion and their worldly life, in what is immediate and in what is deferred. {They will have a collar of what they were stingy with placed around their necks on the Day of Resurrection}; that is, what they were stingy with will be made into a collar around their necks, by which they will be punished, as is stated in the sound hadith: "Indeed, the miser's wealth will be represented to him on the Day of Resurrection as a bald poisonous snake with two black spots over its eyes, which will seize him by his jaws and say: 'I am your wealth, I am your treasure.'" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then recited this verse as confirmation of it. These people thought that their stinginess would benefit them and bring them gain, but the matter was reversed against them, and it became one of the greatest harms to them and the cause of their punishment. {And to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth}; that is, He, exalted is He, is the Owner of sovereignty, and all possessions return to their owner, and the servants depart from the world with no dirham, no dinar, and no other wealth with them. Allah, the Exalted, says: {Indeed, it is We who inherit the earth and whoever is upon it, and to Us they will be returned}. Reflect on how He mentioned the initial cause and the final cause, each of which requires that the servant not be stingy with what Allah has given him.

He first informed that what is in the servant's possession and hand is a bounty and favour from Allah, not a possession of the servant; indeed, were it not for Allah's bounty and kindness upon him, nothing of it would have reached him. So withholding it is withholding the bounty and kindness of Allah. Moreover, His kindness requires that one be kind to His servants, as He said: {And do good as Allah has done good to you}. Whoever is certain that what is in his hand is a bounty from Allah will not withhold the bounty that does not harm him; rather, it benefits him in his heart, his wealth, the increase of his faith, and his protection from calamities.

Second, He mentioned that what is in the hands of the servants all returns to Allah, and He inherits it, and He is the best of inheritors. There is no sense in being stingy with something that is departing from you and passing to another.

Third, He mentioned the recompensatory cause, saying: {And Allah is Aware of what you do}. Since He is Aware of all your deeds, this entails good reward for good deeds and punishment for evil. Whoever has in his heart an atom's weight of faith will not refrain from the spending that is rewarded, nor be content with the withholding that brings punishment.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 3, verses 181–182:

{181} He, exalted is He, informs about the statement of those rebellious people who uttered the most abominable, most vile and most disgraceful speech. He informs that He has indeed heard what they said, and that He will record it and preserve it along with their monstrous deeds, namely their killing of the sincere prophets. He will punish them for that with the most severe punishment, and it will be said to them, in place of their saying "Indeed Allah is poor and we are rich": ﴿Taste the punishment of the burning Fire﴾; the burning one that penetrates from the body to the hearts. Their punishment is not an injustice from Allah toward them, for ﴿He is not ever unjust to the servants﴾; for He is exalted above that.

{182} ﴿That is for what your hands have put forth﴾; that is, the disgraceful and vile deeds which necessitated their deserving the punishment and their being deprived of reward. The exegetes have mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning a group of Jews who spoke these words, and they named among them Finhas ibn Azura, one of the leading scholars of the Jews in Medina. When he heard the words of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan?﴾ and ﴿And lend Allah a goodly loan﴾, he said, out of arrogance and insolence, this statement, may Allah curse him. Allah related it from them and informed that it was not an innovation of their abominations, rather there had preceded from them abominations of a similar kind, namely their killing of the prophets without right. This restriction is intended to indicate that they dared to kill them while knowing its monstrousness, not out of ignorance and misguidance, but out of rebellion and obstinacy.

{181} He, exalted is He, informs about the statement of those rebellious people who uttered the most abominable, most vile and most disgraceful speech. He will punish them for that with the most severe punishment, and it will be said to them, in place of their saying "Indeed Allah is poor and we are rich": ﴿Taste the punishment of the burning Fire﴾; the burning one that penetrates from the body to the hearts. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 3, verses 183–184:

{183} He, exalted is He, informs us about the state of these fabricators who say: ﴿Indeed, Allah has taken our covenant﴾; that is, He commanded us in advance and enjoined us that we should not believe in any messenger until he brings us an offering that fire consumes. Thus they combined lying against Allah and restricting the sign of the messengers to what they had said of this manifest falsehood. And they claim that if they do not believe in a messenger who fails to bring them an offering that fire consumes, then in this they are obedient to their Lord and bound by His covenant. Yet it is known that every messenger whom Allah sends is supported with signs and proofs of the kind by which mankind has believed, and He did not confine them to what they had said. Despite this, they uttered a lie that they did not adhere to and a falsehood they did not act upon. For this reason Allah commanded His Messenger to say to them: ﴿Say: "Messengers before me have certainly come to you with clear proofs and with what you speak of, so why did you kill them, if you are truthful?"﴾; that is, in your claim of believing in a messenger who brings you an offering that fire consumes. Thus their lying, their obstinacy and their contradiction have become clear.

{184} Then He consoled His Messenger, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, saying: ﴿And if they deny you, [O Muhammad], then messengers before you were denied﴾; that is, this is the habit of the wrongdoers and their custom: disbelief in Allah and denial of the messengers of Allah. Their denial of the messengers of Allah is not due to deficiency in what they brought, nor to the absence of a clear proof, but rather they ﴿came with clear proofs﴾; that is, rational arguments and transmitted evidences, ﴿and the scriptures﴾; that is, the written books sent down from heaven, which no one other than messengers could bring, ﴿and the enlightening Book﴾, clarifying the legal rulings and explaining the rational excellences they contain, and also illuminating true reports. So if this has been their habit in disbelieving messengers who are described thus, then let not their affair grieve you, nor their matter concern you. Then Allah, exalted is He, said:

{185} This noble verse contains a call to renounce the world (al-tazhid fi al-dunya), by [pointing to] its passing away and its non-permanence, and that it is "the enjoyment of delusion" (mata' al-ghurur). It tempts with its adornment, deceives with its delusion, and beguiles with its attractions. Then it is transient, and one moves away from it toward the abode of permanence (dar al-qarar), in which souls are repaid for whatever good and evil they did in this abode. ﴿Whoever is drawn away﴾; i.e., removed ﴿from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has truly succeeded﴾; i.e., he has attained the great success, by being saved from painful punishment and reaching the gardens of bliss, in which is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.

The implication of the verse is that whoever is not drawn away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has not succeeded; rather, he has ended in everlasting wretchedness and has been afflicted with endless punishment.

In this verse there is also a subtle allusion to the bliss and punishment of the barzakh (the intermediate state), and that the doers are recompensed in it with some of the recompense for what they did, and a sample of what they sent ahead is presented to them. This is understood from His words: ﴿Indeed, you will only be given your full reward on the Day of Resurrection﴾; i.e., the complete fulfillment of deeds occurs on the Day of Resurrection, while what is short of that occurs in the barzakh, and indeed it may occur even before that, in this world, as in His words: ﴿And We will surely let them taste the nearer punishment short of the greater punishment﴾.

{186} He, exalted is He, informs and addresses the believers that they will be tested in their wealth, through obligatory and voluntary expenditures and through being exposed to its loss in the way of Allah, and in their selves, through being charged with the heavy burdens of obligations that are weighty for many people, such as striving in the way of Allah, with its exposure to fatigue, killing, captivity and wounds, and such as the illnesses that afflict a person in himself or in one he loves. "And you will surely hear from those who were given the Scripture and from the polytheists much hurt." That is, the reviling of you, of your religion, of your Scripture and of your Messenger. In His informing His servant believers of this there are several benefits:

First: His wisdom requires this, so that the true believer may be distinguished from others.

Second: He, exalted is He, decrees these matters upon them for the good He intends for them, to raise their ranks, to expiate their misdeeds, and so that their faith may increase thereby and their certainty be completed. For when He informs them of it and it happens as He said, they say: "This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us, and Allah and His Messenger have spoken truly," and it only increased them in faith and submission.

Third: He informed them of this so that their souls would settle into the occurrence of these things and into patience with them when they occur, since they have prepared themselves for their occurrence; thus their burden becomes lighter for them and their hardship eases, and they take refuge in patience and piety. For this reason He said: "But if you are patient and fear Allah," that is: if you are patient over what has befallen you in your wealth and your selves of trial and testing, and over the harm of the wrongdoers, and you fear Allah regarding that patience by intending thereby the face of Allah and nearness to Him, and you do not exceed in your patience the legal limit of patience in a situation where forbearance is not permitted for you; rather, your duty therein is to take retribution against the enemies of Allah. "Indeed, that is of the matters requiring resolve." That is: of the matters upon which one resolves and competes, and which are not granted except to the people of resolve and lofty aspirations, as He, exalted is He, said: "And none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one of great fortune."

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 3, verses 187–188:

{187} Al-Mithaq (the covenant) is a heavy, firmly binding pledge. God Most High took this covenant from everyone to whom He gave the Scriptures and whom He taught knowledge: that they should make clear to people what they need of what God has taught them, not conceal it from them, and not withhold it from them, especially when they ask or when something arises that requires it. For everyone who has knowledge is obligated, in such a situation, to make it clear and to make the truth distinct from falsehood. As for those who are granted success, they uphold this fully, teaching people what God has taught them, seeking the pleasure of their Lord, out of compassion for creation, and out of fear of the sin of concealment. But as for those who were given the Book, the Jews and Christians and those who resemble them, they cast these covenants and pledges behind their backs and paid them no heed. They concealed the truth and displayed falsehood, boldly transgressing what God has forbidden and carelessly disregarding His rights and the rights of His creation, and they exchanged that concealment ﴿for a small price﴾, which is whatever little accrues to them of some leadership and worthless wealth from their lowly followers who obey their desires and prefer their appetites over the truth. ﴿Wretched is what they barter﴾, because the exchange is most base, while what they turned away from, namely making the truth clear, which holds everlasting happiness and religious and worldly benefits, is the greatest and most noble of aims. They chose the lowly and despicable over the lofty and precious only because of their own misfortune, their baseness, and their being unfit for anything other than what they were created for. Then God Most High said:

{188} ﴿Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have brought﴾; that is, of ugly deeds and falsehood, whether in speech or action, ﴿and love to be praised for what they did not do﴾; that is, for good they did not do and truth they did not speak. Thus they combined the commission of evil, speaking it, rejoicing in it, and loving to be praised for good deeds they never performed. ﴿Do not think them safe from the punishment﴾; that is, in a place of escape from it and safety. Rather, they deserve it and will surely arrive at it, and for this reason He said: ﴿and for them is a painful punishment﴾.
This noble verse includes the People of the Book who rejoiced in the knowledge they had and did not submit to the Messenger, and claimed that they were the ones in the right in their state and their statements. It likewise includes everyone who innovates a bid'ah (innovation) in speech or action, rejoices in it, calls to it, and claims that he is right and that others are wrong, as is the reality among the people of innovation.
The verse also indicates, by its implication, that whoever loves to be praised and commended for the good he has done and for following the truth, provided that his intention in this is not showing off (riya') or seeking reputation, is not blameworthy. Rather, this is among the desirable matters by which God has informed that He rewards those who do good in deeds and words, and by which He has rewarded His elect among His creation, who asked Him for it, as Abraham, peace be upon him, said: ﴿And grant me a tongue of truth among the later generations﴾, and He said: ﴿Peace upon Noah among the worlds. Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good﴾. The servants of the Most Merciful have also said: ﴿and make us leaders for the righteous﴾. This is among the blessings of the Creator upon His servant and His favors, which require gratitude.

{189} That is: He is the Owner of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them of all kinds of creation, the One who disposes of them with perfect power and wondrous craftsmanship. None of them can escape Him, and none can overpower Him.

{190} Allah, may He be exalted, informs: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding﴾. Within this is an exhortation to the servants to reflect upon them, to observe their signs carefully, and to contemplate their creation. He left the word ﴿signs﴾ indefinite and did not specify a particular aspect, indicating their abundance and comprehensiveness. Among them are wondrous signs that amaze the observers, satisfy those who reflect, attract the hearts of the sincere, and awaken luminous minds to all the divine truths. As for the detailed account of what they contain, no created being can encompass it or comprehend even part of it. In sum, the greatness, vastness, and orderly motion and movement found in them indicate the greatness of their Creator, the greatness of His dominion, and the all-encompassing reach of His power. The precision, perfection, wondrous craftsmanship, and subtle workmanship found in them indicate the wisdom of Allah and His placing of things in their proper places, and the vastness of His knowledge. The benefits they provide for creation indicate the vastness of Allah's mercy, the generality of His bounty, the comprehensiveness of His kindness, and the obligation to thank Him. All of this indicates that the heart should be attached to their Creator and Originator, and that one should exert effort in seeking His pleasure, and not associate anything with Him from among those who possess neither for themselves nor for others an atom's weight in the earth or in the heavens. Allah specified ﴿those of understanding﴾ for the signs, and they are the people of intellect, because they are the ones who benefit from them and who look at them with their intellects, not merely with their eyes.

{191} Then He described those of understanding as: ﴿those who remember Allah, standing, sitting, and on their sides﴾. This includes all types of remembrance, by tongue and by heart, and it includes prayer: one prays standing, and if unable, sitting, and if unable, lying on one's side. And [they are] ﴿those who reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾; that is, so that they may be guided by them to the purpose for which they were created. This indicates that reflection is an act of worship and one of the attributes of the knowing friends of Allah. When they reflect upon them, they realize that Allah did not create them in vain, so they say: ﴿Our Lord, You did not create this in vain; glory be to You﴾, exalted above everything unbefitting Your majesty, ﴿but [You created it] in truth﴾ and for truth, rather, You created it containing truth, ﴿so protect us from the punishment of the Fire﴾, by preserving us from evil deeds and enabling us to do righteous deeds, so that by that we may attain salvation from the Fire. This implicitly includes asking for Paradise, because when Allah protects them from the punishment of the Fire, Paradise is attained for them. But since fear has settled in their hearts, they supplicate to Allah with what is most important to them:

{192} ﴿Our Lord, indeed whoever You cause to enter the Fire, You have disgraced him﴾; that is, because he has incurred the wrath of Allah, His angels, and His friends, and falls into a disgrace from which there is no escape and no one to rescue him. Therefore He said: ﴿And for the wrongdoers there are no helpers﴾, who could rescue them from His punishment. And this indicates that they entered it because of their wrongdoing.

{193} ﴿Our Lord, indeed we heard a caller calling to faith﴾, and he is Muhammad (ﷺ); [i.e.] he calls people to it and encourages them to it in its roots and branches. ﴿So we believed﴾; that is, we responded to him promptly and hastened to it. In this there is an acknowledgment from them of Allah's favor upon them, a expression of pride in His blessing, and a means of seeking through it that He forgive their sins and expiate their evil deeds, because good deeds remove evil deeds. The One who bestowed upon them faith will surely bestow upon them complete security. ﴿And cause us to die with the righteous﴾. This supplication includes the request for success in doing good and abandoning evil, by which the servant becomes one of the righteous, and for persistence in that and steadfastness until death.

{194} When they mentioned Allah's granting them success in faith and their seeking means through it to the completion of blessing, they asked Him for reward for that, and that He fulfill for them what He promised them through His messengers of victory and supremacy in this world, and success in the good pleasure of Allah and His Paradise in the Hereafter, for indeed He, may He be exalted, does not break His promise. So Allah answered their supplication and accepted their humble entreaty, and therefore He said:

Therefore He said: ﴿And for the wrongdoers there are no helpers﴾, who could rescue them from His punishment. And this indicates that they entered it because of their wrongdoing.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 3, verse 195:

{195} That is: Allah answered their supplication, both the supplication of worship and the supplication of request, and said: ﴿Indeed, I will not allow to be lost the work of any worker among you, whether male or female.﴾ So all of them will receive the reward of their deeds in full and complete measure. That is, you are all equal in reward and punishment. ﴿So those who emigrated and were expelled from their homes and harmed in My cause and fought and were killed﴾ combined faith, emigration, and leaving behind beloved things of homeland and wealth, seeking the good pleasure of their Lord, and striving in the cause of Allah. ﴿Surely I will remove from them their misdeeds and admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow as a reward from Allah.﴾ He gives His servant a great reward for a small deed. ﴿And with Allah is the best reward﴾, which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no thought has occurred to the heart of a human being. So whoever wants that should seek it from Allah by obeying Him and drawing near to Him with what the servant is able to do.

{196} This verse is intended to console (the believers) regarding what the disbelievers obtain of the enjoyments of this world and their luxury therein, and their moving about in the lands with various kinds of trade, gain, pleasures, and various forms of honor and dominance at certain times. Indeed, all of this:

{197} {A brief enjoyment} has no permanence and no lasting existence. Rather, they enjoy it for a little while and are punished for it for a long time. This is the highest state that a disbeliever can attain, and you have seen what it leads to.

{198} As for those who are mindful of their Lord, who believe in Him, then in addition to what they obtain of the honor and bliss of this world, {for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever}. Thus, even if it were supposed that in the abode of this world they experienced every kind of misery, hardship, toil, and difficulty, this would be, compared to the lasting bliss, the sound life, the joy, the delight, and the happiness, a small and meager thing, and a gift in the form of a trial. For this reason the Exalted said: {And what is with Allah is better for the righteous}, namely those whose hearts are dutiful, so their words and actions are dutiful, and so the Dutiful, the Merciful, rewards them from His kindness with a great reward, a bountiful gift, and everlasting success.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 3, verse 199–200:

{199} That is: ﴿And indeed among the People of the Book are those who believe in Allah and in what has been revealed to you and what has been revealed to them﴾, a group granted success in goodness. This is beneficial faith, unlike that of one who believes in some of the messengers and books and disbelieves in others. Therefore, since their faith was comprehensive and genuine, it became beneficial, and it produced in them the fear of Allah and submission to His majesty, which necessitates compliance with His commands and prohibitions and standing at His limits. These are the People of the Book and knowledge in reality, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Only those of His servants who have knowledge fear Allah﴾. And among the completeness of their fear of Allah is that they ﴿do not exchange the signs of Allah for a small price﴾, so they do not prefer this world over the religion, as did the people of deviation who conceal what Allah has revealed and take for it a small price. As for these, they recognized the matter in reality and knew that among the greatest losses is being content with what is base in place of the religion, and adhering to some base portions of the self and abandoning the truth, which is the greatest portion and success in this world and the Hereafter. So they preferred the truth, clarified it, called to it, and warned against falsehood. Allah rewarded them for that by promising them a great reward and a beautiful recompense, and informed them of His nearness and that He is ﴿swift in reckoning﴾, so they should not be impatient for what Allah has promised, because what is coming is certain to occur, so it is near.

{200} Then He urged the believers to that which leads them to success (al-falah), which is attaining happiness and triumph, and that the path leading to that is adherence to patience (al-sabr), which is restraining the self from what it dislikes, such as abandoning sins, and enduring calamities and burdensome commands upon the souls. So He commanded them to be patient in all of that. Al-musabarah (perseverance-contest) is constancy and continuity in that at all times, and confronting the enemies in all circumstances. Al-murabatah (steadfast garrisoning) is adhering to the place from which the enemy's arrival is feared, and watching over their enemies and preventing them from reaching their aims. ﴿So that you may succeed﴾: they will attain what is loved in religion, worldly life, and the Hereafter, and be saved from what is disliked likewise. It is thus known that there is no way to success without the patience, perseverance, and steadfast garrisoning mentioned; no one has succeeded except by them, and no one has failed to attain success except by neglecting them or some of them.

And Allah is the Granter of success, and there is no power nor strength except with Him.

The commentary on Surat Al 'Imran is complete. All praise is due to Allah for His blessing, and we ask Him to complete the blessing.
